studyNotes.content:
# Magento 2: Module File Structure & Registration
## Study Notes — Week 1, Day 1 | Architecture

---

## Table of Contents

1. [Module Anatomy Overview](#1-module-anatomy-overview)
2. [registration.php — ComponentRegistrar](#2-registrationphp--componentregistrar)
3. [module.xml — Module Declaration](#3-modulexml--module-declaration)
4. [composer.json — Autoloading & Type](#4-composerjson--autoloading--type)
5. [The etc/ Directory — Area-Based Loading](#5-the-etc-directory--area-based-loading)
6. [Module Sequence & Dependency Ordering](#6-module-sequence--dependency-ordering)
7. [Module Enable/Disable Lifecycle](#7-module-enabledisable-lifecycle)
8. [Vendor_Namespace Conventions](#8-vendornamespace-conventions)
9. [Hands-On: Exploring vendor/magento/module-catalog/](#9-hands-on-exploring-vendormagentommodule-catalog)
10. [Custom Module Reference Structure](#10-custom-module-reference-structure)
11. [Quick-Reference Checklist](#quick-reference-checklist)

---

## 1. Module Anatomy Overview

A Magento 2 module is a **self-contained unit of business logic** grouped under a single directory. Every module must have a minimum set of files to be recognized by the framework.

```
app/code/Vendor/ModuleName/
|-- registration.php          <-- Tells Magento this directory is a module
|-- etc/
|   |-- module.xml            <-- Declares module name, version, dependencies
|-- composer.json             <-- (Optional for app/code, required for vendor/)
```

> **Exam focus:** The **minimum required files** for a working module are `registration.php` and `etc/module.xml`. Without either, Magento will not recognize the module.

### Module Locations

| Location | Purpose | Registration Method |
|---|---|---|
| `app/code/Vendor/Module/` | Custom / project modules | `registration.php` |
| `vendor/vendor-name/module-name/` | Composer-installed modules | `registration.php` auto-loaded via Composer |
| `app/code/` (generated) | Rarely used for core | Same as custom |

---

## 2. registration.php — ComponentRegistrar

The `registration.php` file is the **entry point** for module discovery. It is loaded by Magento's autoloader during bootstrap and registers the module's filesystem path.

### Minimal registration.php

```php
<?php
use Magento\Framework\Component\ComponentRegistrar;

ComponentRegistrar::register(
    ComponentRegistrar::MODULE,   // Component type constant
    'Vendor_ModuleName',          // Module name in Vendor_Module format
    __DIR__                       // Absolute path to the module root
);
```

### ComponentRegistrar Component Types

```php
// All valid component type constants:
ComponentRegistrar::MODULE     // 'module'
ComponentRegistrar::THEME      // 'theme'
ComponentRegistrar::LANGUAGE   // 'language'
ComponentRegistrar::LIBRARY    // 'library'
ComponentRegistrar::SETUP      // 'setup'
```

> **Exam focus:** The first argument to `ComponentRegistrar::register()` determines the **component type**. For modules it is always `ComponentRegistrar::MODULE`. Know all five constants — the four most common are MODULE, THEME, LANGUAGE, and LIBRARY; SETUP is used internally for setup modules.

### How registration.php Gets Loaded

```
Composer autoload (vendor/autoload.php)
        |
        v
app/etc/registration_globlist.php
        |
        v  (glob pattern: app/code/*/*/registration.php)
        |
        v
Each registration.php is require()'d
        |
        v
ComponentRegistrar stores [name => path] map in memory
```

> **Exam focus:** For `app/code` modules, Magento uses a **glob pattern** (`app/code/*/*/registration.php`) defined in `app/etc/registration_globlist.php` to find all registrations automatically. You do **not** need to manually add entries to any list for `app/code`.

### Registration for Composer-Installed Modules

In `composer.json`, the autoload section ensures `registration.php` is included:

```json
"autoload": {
    "files": ["registration.php"],
    "psr-4": {
        "Vendor\\ModuleName\\": ""
    }
}
```

---

## 3. module.xml — Module Declaration

Located at `etc/module.xml`, this file formally declares the module to the Magento system — its **name**, **setup version**, and **load sequence dependencies**.

### Full module.xml Structure

```xml
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<config xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:Module/etc/module.xsd">
    <module name="Vendor_ModuleName" setup_version="1.0.0">
        <sequence>
            <module name="Magento_Catalog"/>
            <module name="Magento_Customer"/>
        </sequence>
    </module>
</config>
```

### Attribute Reference

| Attribute | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | **Yes** | Module identifier. Must match `registration.php`. Format: `Vendor_ModuleName` |
| `setup_version` | No* | Used by upgrade scripts (`InstallSchema`, `UpgradeData`, etc.). Omit for declarative schema only |
| `<sequence>` | No | Declares load-order dependencies (covered in Section 6) |

> **Exam focus:** The `name` attribute in `module.xml` **must exactly match** the name used in `registration.php`. A mismatch causes a module load failure. `setup_version` is deprecated when using **declarative schema** (`db_schema.xml`) but may still appear in legacy modules.

### Schema Validation

The XSD schema is referenced via URN:

```
urn:magento:framework:Module/etc/module.xsd
```

Magento resolves this internally to:
```
vendor/magento/framework/Module/etc/module.xsd
```

---

## 4. composer.json — Autoloading & Type

While optional for `app/code` modules during development, `composer.json` is **required** for any module distributed via Packagist or installed through Composer.

### Full composer.json for a Module

```json
{
    "name": "vendor/module-name",
    "description": "Description of the module",
    "type": "magento2-module",
    "version": "1.0.0",
    "require": {
        "php": "~8.1.0||~8.2.0",
        "magento/framework": "*",
        "magento/module-catalog": "*"
    },
    "autoload": {
        "files": [
            "registration.php"
        ],
        "psr-4": {
            "Vendor\\ModuleName\\": ""
        }
    },
    "extra": {
        "map": [
            ["*", "Vendor/ModuleName"]
        ]
    }
}
```

### Key Fields Explained

| Field | Value | Importance |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | `"magento2-module"` | Tells Composer/Magento installer what kind of component this is |
| `autoload.files` | `["registration.php"]` | Ensures registration runs on every Composer autoload |
| `autoload.psr-4` | `"Vendor\\ModuleName\\": ""` | Maps namespace to directory root |
| `require` | Dependencies | Ensures correct packages are installed |

> **Exam focus:** The `type` field **must be** `"magento2-module"` for Magento modules. Other valid types include `magento2-theme`, `magento2-language`, `magento2-library`. The PSR-4 key uses **double backslash** (`\\`) in JSON.

### PSR-4 Autoloading Logic

```
Namespace:   Vendor\ModuleName\Model\Product
                    |
                    v  (strip "Vendor\ModuleName\", prepend module root)
File path:   app/code/Vendor/ModuleName/Model/Product.php
```

---

## 5. The etc/ Directory — Area-Based Loading

The `etc/` directory is the **configuration hub** of a module. Magento uses an **area-based loading system** to merge configuration files selectively based on the current execution context.

### Area Hierarchy

```
etc/
|-- module.xml              (always loaded - module declaration)
|-- di.xml                  (global scope DI config)
|-- events.xml              (global scope events)
|-- routes.xml              (N/A at global - see below)
|-- acl.xml                 (global - ACL resources)
|-- config.xml              (global - system configuration defaults)
|-- crontab.xml             (global - cron job definitions)
|-- db_schema.xml           (global - declarative schema)
|-- email_templates.xml     (global - transactional email templates)
|-- frontend/
|   |-- di.xml              (frontend area only)
|   |-- events.xml          (frontend area only)
|   |-- routes.xml          (frontend router config)
|   |-- sections.xml        (customer data sections)
|   |-- page_types.xml      (frontend page types)
|   |-- layout/             (layout XML files)
|-- adminhtml/
|   |-- di.xml              (adminhtml area only)
|   |-- events.xml          (adminhtml area only)
|   |-- routes.xml          (admin router config)
|   |-- menu.xml            (admin menu items)
|   |-- system.xml          (system configuration fields)
|-- webapi_rest/
|   |-- di.xml              (REST API area only)
|-- webapi_soap/
|   |-- di.xml              (SOAP API area only)
|-- graphql/
    |-- di.xml              (GraphQL area only)
```

### Area Loading Rules

> **Exam focus:** Configuration files are loaded in a **two-pass merge**: first `etc/` (global), then `etc/{area}/` (area-specific). Area-specific config **overrides or extends** global config of the same filename. The merge strategy differs by file type.

| Area | Constant | URL Pattern | When Active |
|---|---|---|---|
| `global` | `Area::AREA_GLOBAL` | N/A | CLI, setup, cron |
| `frontend` | `Area::AREA_FRONTEND` | `domain.com/` | Storefront requests |
| `adminhtml` | `Area::AREA_ADMINHTML` | `domain.com/admin/` | Admin panel requests |
| `webapi_rest` | `Area::AREA_WEBAPI_REST` | `domain.com/rest/` | REST API requests |
| `webapi_soap` | `Area::AREA_WEBAPI_SOAP` | `domain.com/soap/` | SOAP API requests |
| `graphql` | `Area::AREA_GRAPHQL` | `domain.com/graphql` | GraphQL requests |

### di.xml — Dependency Injection Config

```xml
<!-- etc/di.xml (global) -->
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<config xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:ObjectManager/etc/config.xsd">

    <!-- Type preference (interface -> implementation) -->
    <preference for="Vendor\ModuleName\Api\DataInterface"
                type="Vendor\ModuleName\Model\Data"/>

    <!-- Plugin declaration -->
    <type name="Magento\Catalog\Model\Product">
        <plugin name="vendor_module_product_plugin"
                type="Vendor\ModuleName\Plugin\ProductPlugin"
                sortOrder="10"
                disabled="false"/>
    </type>

    <!-- Virtual type -->
    <virtualType name="Vendor\ModuleName\Model\SpecialLogger"
                 type="Magento\Framework\Logger\Monolog">
        <arguments>
            <argument name="name" xsi:type="string">special</argument>
        </arguments>
    </virtualType>

</config>
```

### events.xml — Observer Registration

```xml
<!-- etc/events.xml (global) or etc/frontend/events.xml (frontend only) -->
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<config xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:Event/etc/events.xsd">
    <event name="catalog_product_save_after">
        <observer name="vendor_module_product_save"
                  instance="Vendor\ModuleName\Observer\ProductSaveAfter"/>
    </event>
</config>
```

> **Exam focus:** An observer registered in `etc/events.xml` (global) fires in **all areas**. An observer in `etc/frontend/events.xml` fires **only in frontend**. Use the most restrictive area possible for performance.

### routes.xml — Router Configuration

```xml
<!-- etc/frontend/routes.xml -->
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<config xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:App/etc/routes.xsd">
    <router id="standard">
        <route id="vendor_module" frontName="vendor-module">
            <module name="Vendor_ModuleName"/>
        </route>
    </router>
</config>
```

```xml
<!-- etc/adminhtml/routes.xml -->
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<config xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:App/etc/routes.xsd">
    <router id="admin">
        <route id="vendor_module" frontName="vendor_module">
            <module name="Vendor_ModuleName"/>
        </route>
    </router>
</config>
```

> **Exam focus:** Frontend routes use router `id="standard"`. Admin routes use router `id="admin"`. The `frontName` becomes the first URL segment: `domain.com/{frontName}/controller/action`.

### Configuration File Summary Table

| File | Global | frontend | adminhtml | webapi_rest |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `di.xml` | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| `events.xml` | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| `routes.xml` | No | Yes | Yes | No |
| `system.xml` | No | No | Yes | No |
| `menu.xml` | No | No | Yes | No |
| `sections.xml` | No | Yes | No | No |
| `webapi.xml` | Yes | No | No | No |
| `crontab.xml` | Yes | No | No | No |
| `acl.xml` | Yes | No | No | No |

---

## 6. Module Sequence & Dependency Ordering

### What is Module Sequence?

Module sequence declares the **load order** of modules. It does **not** create hard dependencies (those go in `composer.json` `require`), but tells Magento: *"If module X is enabled, load it before me."*

```xml
<!-- etc/module.xml -->
<module name="Vendor_ModuleName">
    <sequence>
        <module name="Magento_Catalog"/>
        <module name="Magento_Store"/>
    </sequence>
</module>
```

> **Exam focus:** `<sequence>` is a **soft dependency** for ordering. It does NOT enforce that the listed module is installed. For hard dependencies (module must exist), use `composer.json` `require`. For hard Magento-level dependencies, some teams also use both.

### Why Sequence Matters

```
Without sequence:
  ModuleA plugin on ProductModel::save() -> sort order 10
  ModuleB plugin on ProductModel::save() -> sort order 10
  Loading order: UNPREDICTABLE -> race condition on plugin execution

With sequence (ModuleA declares ModuleB in sequence):
  ModuleB config merged FIRST -> ModuleA config merged SECOND
  Plugin from ModuleA evaluated after ModuleB's -> PREDICTABLE
```

### Sequence Affects These Merges

| Config Type | Why Order Matters |
|---|---|
| `di.xml` plugins | Plugin sort order tie-breaking; later module's plugins loaded after earlier's |
| `di.xml` preferences | Later-merged preference wins |
| `events.xml` observers | Observer execution order within same event |
| Layout XML | Later module's layout instructions applied last |
| Template overrides | Path resolution order |

### Sequence vs. Composer `require`

```
composer.json "require"          module.xml <sequence>
---------------------------      ---------------------------
Hard dependency                  Soft ordering hint
Installer enforces it            Framework uses it for merge order
Module won't install without     Module still works without
the required package             the sequenced module (if not enabled)
```

> **Exam focus:** A common exam scenario: *"You want your plugin to run after Magento_Catalog's plugin on the same method. What do you do?"* Answer: Add `Magento_Catalog` to your module's `<sequence>` in `module.xml`.

---

## 7. Module Enable/Disable Lifecycle

### app/etc/config.php — The Module Registry

The file `app/etc/config.php` is the **authoritative list** of enabled/disabled modules. It is auto-generated and should be committed to version control.

```php
<?php
// app/etc/config.php (abbreviated)
return [
    'modules' => [
        'Magento_Store'          => 1,   // 1 = enabled
        'Magento_Catalog'        => 1,
        'Magento_Customer'       => 1,
        'Vendor_ModuleName'      => 1,
        'Some_DisabledModule'    => 0,   // 0 = disabled
    ]
];
```

> **Exam focus:** `app/etc/config.php` stores `1` for enabled and `0` for disabled. This file is **generated** by CLI commands and should be in version control. Do NOT confuse with `app/etc/env.php` (environment-specific, NOT in VCS).

### bin/magento Module Commands

#### Enable a Module

```bash
# Enable one module
bin/magento module:enable Vendor_ModuleName

# Enable with static content deployment cleanup
bin/magento module:enable Vendor_ModuleName --clear-static-content

# Enable multiple modules
bin/magento module:enable Vendor_ModuleA Vendor_ModuleB

# Enable all modules
bin/magento module:enable --all

# Force enable even if dependencies are missing (use with caution)
bin/magento module:enable Vendor_ModuleName --force
```

#### Disable a Module

```bash
# Disable one module
bin/magento module:disable Vendor_ModuleName

# Disable and clear generated static files
bin/magento module:disable Vendor_ModuleName --clear-static-content

# Disable all modules (dangerous in production!)
bin/magento module:disable --all
```

#### List Modules

```bash
# List all modules with status
bin/magento module:status

# List only enabled modules
bin/magento module:status --enabled

# List only disabled modules
bin/magento module:status --disabled

# Check a specific module
bin/magento module:status Vendor_ModuleName
```

### Post-Enable/Disable Required Steps

```bash
# After enabling a module:
bin/magento setup:upgrade              # Run setup scripts / schema
bin/magento setup:di:compile           # Regenerate DI config
bin/magento cache:flush                # Clear all caches

# After disabling a module:
bin/magento cache:flush
# Optionally:
bin/magento setup:di:compile
```

> **Exam focus:** `--clear-static-content` flag removes files from `pub/static/`. This is needed when a module adds static assets (JS, CSS) to avoid stale cached files being served. Both `module:enable` and `module:disable` support `--clear-static-content`, `--all`, and `--force`.

### Module Lifecycle States

```
Not registered                 Registered only
(no registration.php)          (registration.php exists,
         |                      not in config.php)
         |                             |
         v                             v
   Not discovered              "unrecognized" state
                                       |
                                       v
                              bin/magento module:enable
                                       |
                                       v
                              config.php entry = 1        (ENABLED)
                                       |
                                       v
                              bin/magento setup:upgrade
                                       |
                                       v
                              Schema/Data installed       (ACTIVE)
                                       |
                                       v
                              bin/magento module:disable
                                       |
                                       v
                              config.php entry = 0        (DISABLED)
```

### Uninstalling a Module

```bash
# Full uninstall (runs uninstall scripts, removes from composer)
bin/magento module:uninstall Vendor_ModuleName

# Remove DB data and schema created by module
bin/magento module:uninstall Vendor_ModuleName --remove-data

# Non-composer module (app/code) - just disable, then manually delete
bin/magento module:disable Vendor_ModuleName
rm -rf app/code/Vendor/ModuleName/
bin/magento setup:upgrade
```

---

## 8. Vendor_Namespace Conventions

### Naming Rules

| Component | Rule | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Vendor name | PascalCase, no underscores | `Magento`, `Acme`, `MyCompany` |
| Module name | PascalCase, no underscores | `Catalog`, `CustomerGraphQl`, `SalesRule` |
| Combined | `Vendor_ModuleName` | `Magento_Catalog`, `Acme_Inventory` |
| PHP namespace | `Vendor\ModuleName` | `Magento\Catalog` |
| Composer package | `vendor/module-name` (kebab-case) | `magento/module-catalog` |
| Directory (app/code) | `Vendor/ModuleName` | `Magento/Catalog` |
| Directory (vendor/) | `vendor/module-name` | `magento/module-catalog` |

> **Exam focus:** The module name uses **underscore** as separator in XML/PHP (`Vendor_Module`), **backslash** in PHP namespaces (`Vendor\Module`), and **hyphen** in Composer package names (`vendor/module-name`). These are three different representations of the same module.

### GraphQL Module Naming Convention

```
Magento_CatalogGraphQl   <- Note the capital Q and lowercase l
Magento_CustomerGraphQl
Magento_BundleGraphQl
```

### Real-World Examples from Magento Core

```
Module Name (XML)         PHP Namespace              Composer Package
-----------------         -------------              ----------------
Magento_Catalog           Magento\Catalog            magento/module-catalog
Magento_SalesRule         Magento\SalesRule          magento/module-sales-rule
Magento_ConfigurableProduct  Magento\ConfigurableProduct  magento/module-configurable-product
Magento_CustomerGraphQl   Magento\CustomerGraphQl    magento/module-customer-graph-ql
```

---

## 9. Hands-On: Exploring vendor/magento/module-catalog/

### Directory Exploration Commands

```bash
# List top-level structure
ls -la vendor/magento/module-catalog/

# List all etc/ XML files
find vendor/magento/module-catalog/etc -name "*.xml" | sort

# Count files by type
find vendor/magento/module-catalog/ -name "*.php" | wc -l
find vendor/magento/module-catalog/ -name "*.xml" | wc -l

# View the module.xml
cat vendor/magento/module-catalog/etc/module.xml

# View registration.php
cat vendor/magento/module-catalog/registration.php

# View etc/ directory tree (if tree command available)
tree vendor/magento/module-catalog/etc/
```

### Expected Output of etc/ Exploration

```
vendor/magento/module-catalog/etc/
|-- acl.xml
|-- catalog_attributes.xml
|-- communication.xml
|-- config.xml
|-- crontab.xml
|-- db_schema.xml
|-- di.xml
|-- eav_attributes.xml
|-- events.xml
|-- extension_attributes.xml
|-- indexer.xml
|-- module.xml
|-- mview.xml
|-- product_options.xml
|-- product_types.xml
|-- queue.xml
|-- queue_consumer.xml
|-- queue_publisher.xml
|-- queue_topology.xml
|-- view.xml
|-- webapi.xml
|-- webapi_async.xml
|-- adminhtml/
|   |-- di.xml
|   |-- events.xml
|   |-- menu.xml
|   |-- routes.xml
|   |-- system.xml
|-- frontend/
|   |-- di.xml
|   |-- events.xml
|   |-- page_types.xml
|   |-- routes.xml
|   |-- sections.xml
|-- webapi_rest/
|   |-- di.xml
|-- webapi_soap/
    |-- di.xml
```

### Catalog module.xml — Analyze Its Dependencies

```bash
cat vendor/magento/module-catalog/etc/module.xml
```

```xml
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<config xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:Module/etc/module.xsd">
    <module name="Magento_Catalog">
        <sequence>
            <module name="Magento_Eav"/>
            <module name="Magento_Cms"/>
            <module name="Magento_Indexer"/>
            <module name="Magento_Customer"/>
        </sequence>
    </module>
</config>
```

> **Exam focus:** Notice `Magento_Catalog` has **no `setup_version`** in modern Magento — it uses declarative schema (`db_schema.xml`) exclusively. Older/legacy modules still use `setup_version`. Its sequence dependencies are Eav, Cms, Indexer, and Customer — meaning those modules' configurations are merged before Catalog's.

---

## 10. Custom Module Reference Structure

### Minimal Module (Two Files)

```
app/code/Acme/HelloWorld/
|-- registration.php
|-- etc/
    |-- module.xml
```

### Standard Custom Module (Full Structure)

```

|-- registration.php
|-- composer.json
|-- etc/

|   |-- events.xml

|   |-- config.xml
|   |-- db_schema.xml
|   |-- db_schema_whitelist.json
|   |-- frontend/
|   |   |-- di.xml
|   |   |-- events.xml
|   |   |-- routes.xml
|   |   |-- sections.xml
|   |-- adminhtml/
|       |-- di.xml
|       |-- events.xml
|       |-- routes.xml
|       |-- menu.xml
|       |-- system.xml

|-- Block/

|-- view/
```
