## 3. Observers & Events

Observers use a **publish-subscribe** (pub/sub) pattern. The event manager dispatches named events; registered observers react to them.

### 3.1 Event Dispatch

```php
<?php
namespace Vendor\Module\Model;

use Magento\Framework\Event\ManagerInterface;

class SomeModel
{
    private ManagerInterface $eventManager;

    public function __construct(ManagerInterface $eventManager)
    {
        $this->eventManager = $eventManager;
    }

    public function doSomething(): void
    {
        // Dispatch an event with optional data payload
        $this->eventManager->dispatch(
            'vendor_module_something_happened',   // Event name (snake_case)
            [
                'object'  => $this,              // Data accessible in observer
                'value'   => 'some_value',
            ]
        );
    }
}
```

**Exam focus:**
- Event names are **snake_case** strings.
- The second parameter is an array — it becomes accessible on both the `Event` object AND the `Observer` wrapper (both receive the data array).
- `dispatch()` is fire-and-forget — the return value is `void`; observers cannot modify data returned to the dispatcher.
- Core uses `$this->_eventManager->dispatch(...)` in abstract classes (protected property from `\Magento\Framework\Model\AbstractModel`).

---

### 3.2 Observer Declaration in events.xml

Observers are declared per-area in `<module>/etc/events.xml` or area-specific files.

```xml
<!-- File: app/code/Vendor/Module/etc/events.xml (global) -->
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<config xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:Event/etc/events.xsd">

    <event name="catalog_product_save_after">
        <observer name="vendor_module_product_save_after_observer"
                  instance="Vendor\Module\Observer\ProductSaveAfter"
                  disabled="false"
                  shared="true"/>
    </event>

</config>
```

#### Observer Attribute Reference

| Attribute | Required | Description |
|-----------|----------|-------------|
| `name` | Yes | Unique name within this event scope |
| `instance` | No | Fully-qualified observer class name (optional in XSD) |
| `disabled` | No | `true` to disable a previously declared observer |
| `shared` | No | `true` (default) = singleton; `false` = new instance per dispatch |

**Area-specific files:**

| File Path | Scope |
|-----------|-------|
| `etc/events.xml` | Global (all areas) |
| `etc/frontend/events.xml` | Frontend only |
| `etc/adminhtml/events.xml` | Admin only |
| `etc/crontab/events.xml` | Cron scope |
| `etc/webapi_rest/events.xml` | REST API scope |

**Exam focus:**
- An observer declared in `etc/events.xml` fires in **all areas** including admin, frontend, API.
- To restrict an observer to a specific area, use the area-specific directory.

---

### 3.3 Observer Class Structure

```php
<?php
namespace Vendor\Module\Observer;

use Magento\Framework\Event\Observer;
use Magento\Framework\Event\ObserverInterface;
use Psr\Log\LoggerInterface;

class ProductSaveAfter implements ObserverInterface
{
    private LoggerInterface $logger;

    public function __construct(LoggerInterface $logger)
    {
        $this->logger = $logger;
    }

    /**
     * Execute observer logic.
     *
     * @param Observer $observer
     * @return void
     */
    public function execute(Observer $observer): void
    {
        // Retrieve data passed during dispatch()
        /** @var \Magento\Catalog\Model\Product $product */
        $product = $observer->getEvent()->getProduct();

        // Alternative: getData() from the observer directly (shortcut)
        // $product = $observer->getData('product'); // Also works — data is merged into Observer

        $this->logger->info(
            sprintf('Product saved: %s (ID: %d)', $product->getName(), $product->getId())
        );

        // Observers are VOID — cannot return values to the dispatcher
    }
}
```

> **Note on data access:** Both `$observer->getEvent()->getData('key')` and `$observer->getData('key')` work. In `Manager::dispatch()`, the `$data` array is merged into both the `Event` object AND the `Observer` wrapper (`$wrapper->setData(array_merge(['event' => $event], $data))`).

**Exam focus:**
- Observer class **must** implement `\Magento\Framework\Event\ObserverInterface`.
- The only required method is `execute(Observer $observer): void`.
- Data access: `$observer->getEvent()->getData('key')` or magic getter `$observer->getEvent()->getProduct()`.
- Return values from `execute()` are **ignored** — observers are fire-and-forget.

## 4. Plugins vs Observers — Decision Guide

| Scenario | Use Plugin | Use Observer |
|----------|-----------|--------------|
| Modify method input arguments | Yes (before) | No |
| Modify method return value | Yes (after/around) | No |
| Short-circuit / replace method | Yes (around) | No |
| React after something happens | Possible (after) | Preferred |
| Fire-and-forget notification | No | Yes |
| Decouple modules (event bus) | No | Yes |
| Target a specific method | Yes | No (event-based) |
| Modify 3rd-party class not dispatching events | Yes | No |
| Prevent original execution conditionally | Yes (around) | No |
| Cross-area communication | Possible | Yes |

```
Decision Flow:
                  Need to modify args or return?
                           |
               +-----------+-----------+
               YES                     NO
               |                       |
         Use PLUGIN              React to occurrence?
               |                       |
    +----------+---------+    +--------+--------+
    Modify    Modify     |    YES               NO
    Args      Return   Both   |               (rethink approach)
    |         |         |   Use OBSERVER
  before    after    around
```

**Exam focus:**
- The **key distinction**: Plugins intercept method calls and can alter data flow. Observers listen to events and cannot alter the dispatching code's control flow.
- If you need to modify a return value: **plugin**. If you need to react to an action: **observer**.

```php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vendor\Module\Plugin\Product;

use Magento\Catalog\Model\Product;
use Psr\Log\LoggerInterface;

class BeforeProductSavePlugin
{

    public function __construct(LoggerInterface $logger)
    {
        $this->logger = $logger;
    }

     *
     * Method signature: beforeSave(Product $subject, ...$args)
     * Note: Product::save() takes no arguments, so no extra args here.
     *
     * @param Product $subject
```

## 6. Hands-On: Observer on catalog_product_save_after

### Step 1: Create the Observer Class

```php
<?php
// File: app/code/Vendor/Module/Observer/Product/ProductSaveAfterObserver.php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vendor\Module\Observer\Product;

use Magento\Framework\Event\Observer;
use Magento\Framework\Event\ObserverInterface;
use Psr\Log\LoggerInterface;

class ProductSaveAfterObserver implements ObserverInterface
{
    private LoggerInterface $logger;

    public function __construct(LoggerInterface $logger)
    {
        $this->logger = $logger;
    }

    /**
     * Fired after a product is saved.
     *
     * Event: catalog_product_save_after
     * Event data: 'product' => \Magento\Catalog\Model\Product
     *             'data_object' => \Magento\Catalog\Model\Product (same reference)
     *
     * @param Observer $observer
     * @return void
     */
    public function execute(Observer $observer): void
    {
        /** @var \Magento\Catalog\Model\Product $product */
        $product = $observer->getEvent()->getProduct();

        if (!$product) {
            return;
        }

        // Check if our before plugin fired
        $pluginFired = $product->getData('plugin_before_fired');

        $this->logger->info(sprintf(
            '[ProductSaveAfterObserver] Product saved — Name: "%s", SKU: "%s", Plugin fired: %s',
            $product->getName(),
            $product->getSku(),
            $pluginFired ? 'YES' : 'NO'
        ));

        // Cannot modify the return value of the save() call from here
        // This is fire-and-forget
    }
}
```

## 8. Tricky Exam Scenarios

### Scenario 1: Sort Order Tie-Breaking

```xml
<!-- Module A: Vendor_Alpha, sortOrder=10 -->
<type name="Magento\Catalog\Model\Product">
    <plugin name="alpha_plugin" type="Vendor\Alpha\Plugin\ProductPlugin" sortOrder="10"/>
</type>

<!-- Module B: Vendor_Beta, sortOrder=10 (same!) -->
<type name="Magento\Catalog\Model\Product">
    <plugin name="beta_plugin" type="Vendor\Beta\Plugin\ProductPlugin" sortOrder="10"/>
</type>
```

**Result:** The execution order is **undefined**. The framework uses `uasort` with only the `sortOrder` value as the sort key — there is no secondary key for tie-breaking. The order depends on PHP's internal sort implementation and the array insertion order.

**Exam focus:**
- When two plugins have the same `sortOrder`, the result is **non-deterministic**. Always use distinct `sortOrder` values if execution order matters.
- Plugins without an explicit `sortOrder` default to `0`.

---

### Scenario 2: Around Without $proceed

```php
// BUGGY: Silent chain break
public function aroundGetPrice(Product $subject, callable $proceed): float
{
    if ($this->cache->has($subject->getId())) {
        return $this->cache->get($subject->getId()); // $proceed never called
    }
    // If not cached, falls through... but $proceed is still never called
    // below code is never reached if cache hit, original method never called if no hit
    // This is a logic error!
}

// CORRECT: Proper short-circuit with $proceed fallback
public function aroundGetPrice(Product $subject, callable $proceed): float
{
    if ($this->cache->has($subject->getId())) {
        return $this->cache->get($subject->getId()); // Legitimate short-circuit
    }

    $result = $proceed(); // Original method called when not cached
    $this->cache->set($subject->getId(), $result);
    return $result;
}
```

**Exam focus:**
- Intentional short-circuit (without `$proceed`) is **valid** — e.g., caching, access control.
- Accidental omission of `$proceed` is a silent bug — no exception, no log entry.

---

### Scenario 3: Plugin on Interface vs Concrete Class — Both Declared

```xml
<!-- Plugin on interface -->
<type name="Magento\Catalog\Api\ProductRepositoryInterface">
    <plugin name="interface_plugin" type="..." sortOrder="10"/>
</type>

<!-- Plugin on concrete class -->
<type name="Magento\Catalog\Model\ProductRepository">
    <plugin name="class_plugin" type="..." sortOrder="10"/>
</type>
```

**Result:** Both plugins fire. Interface plugins and class plugins are **additive**, not exclusive.

---

### Scenario 4: Disabled Plugin Override

```xml
<!-- core/etc/di.xml declares: -->
<type name="Magento\Catalog\Model\Product">
    <plugin name="core_expensive_plugin" type="Magento\Core\Plugin\Expensive" sortOrder="5"/>
</type>

<!-- Your module/etc/di.xml disables it: -->
<type name="Magento\Catalog\Model\Product">
    <plugin name="core_expensive_plugin" disabled="true"/>
</type>
```

**Exam focus:**
- Use `disabled="true"` with the **exact same `name` attribute** to disable a plugin declared elsewhere.
- The `type` attribute is not needed when disabling (it's optional in the XSD).

---

### Scenario 5: Observer Area Scope

```xml
<!-- etc/events.xml — fires in ALL areas including cron, API -->
<event name="catalog_product_save_after">
    <observer name="my_observer" instance="..."/>
</event>

<!-- etc/adminhtml/events.xml — fires ONLY in admin -->
<event name="catalog_product_save_after">
    <observer name="my_admin_observer" instance="..."/>
</event>
```

**Exam focus:**
- A global `events.xml` observer fires **everywhere**. This can cause unintended consequences during REST API saves or cron jobs.

---

### Scenario 6: What $observer->getEvent() Returns

```php
public function execute(Observer $observer): void
{
    $event = $observer->getEvent(); // Returns \Magento\Framework\Event

    // Method 1: Magic getter (uses DataObject __call)
    $product = $event->getProduct();          // getData('product')

    // Method 2: Explicit getData
    $product = $event->getData('product');

    // Method 3: From observer directly (shortcut — works because dispatch()
    // merges $data into both the Event and the Observer wrapper)
    $product = $observer->getData('product');
}
```

## 9. Quick-Reference Checklist

### Plugin Fundamentals
- [ ] **Three plugin types:** `before` (modify args), `after` (modify result), `around` (full control)
- [ ] **Before plugin** returns `null` (no change) or `array` (replace positional args)
- [ ] **After plugin** must always return a value; `null` return replaces result with `null`
- [ ] **Around plugin** receives `callable $proceed` as second argument; must call it to continue the chain
- [ ] Plugin method naming: `before{MethodName}`, `after{MethodName}`, `around{MethodName}` (camelCase)

### Plugin Declaration
- [ ] Declared in `<module>/etc/di.xml` or area-specific `etc/<area>/di.xml`
- [ ] `<plugin name="..." type="..." sortOrder="..." disabled="..."/>`
- [ ] `name` = unique per `<type>` block (required); `type` = plugin class FQCN (optional — not needed when disabling)
- [ ] `disabled="true"` with matching `name` disables a previously declared plugin
- [ ] Prefer plugins on **interfaces** over concrete classes

### Plugin Restrictions (Cannot Plugin)
- [ ] `__construct` and `__destruct` — constructors/destructors not interceptable
- [ ] `final` methods or `final` classes
- [ ] `static` methods
- [ ] `protected` or `private` methods (only `public`)
- [ ] `__sleep`, `__wakeup`, `__clone`, `_resetState` — explicitly excluded in interceptor generator
- [ ] Classes implementing `NoninterceptableInterface` (e.g., proxies)
- [ ] Classes not managed by Magento ObjectManager
- [ ] **Note:** `getData()`, `setData()`, `hasData()`, and `__call()` ARE pluggable — they are real public methods

### Sort Order & Execution
- [ ] Lower `sortOrder` = executes **first** for all types (before, after, and around)
- [ ] All plugin types (before, after, around) execute in **ascending** sortOrder
- [ ] Tie-breaking with equal `sortOrder` is **undefined** — always use distinct values
- [ ] Around plugins nest: outer (lower sortOrder) wraps inner (higher sortOrder)
- [ ] Default `sortOrder` when omitted is `0`

### Around Plugin Pitfalls
- [ ] Not calling `$proceed()` silently breaks the chain — **no exception thrown**
- [ ] Intentional short-circuit is valid (caching, auth); accidental omission is a bug
- [ ] Forward args: `$proceed(...$args)` not just `$proceed()`

### Observer Fundamentals
- [ ] Observer class must implement `Magento\Framework\Event\ObserverInterface`
- [ ] Only required method: `execute(Observer $observer): void`
- [ ] `execute()` returns `void`; observers **cannot** modify dispatched data return values
- [ ] Access event data: `$observer->getEvent()->getData('key')` or magic getter `$observer->getEvent()->getProduct()`
- [ ] Shortcut: `$observer->getData('key')` also works (data merged into Observer wrapper)

### Observer Declaration
- [ ] Declared in `<module>/etc/events.xml` (global) or area-specific `etc/<area>/events.xml`
- [ ] `<event name="event_name"><observer name="..." instance="..." disabled="..." shared="..."/></event>`
- [ ] `shared="true"` (default) = singleton via `ObjectManager::get()`; `shared="false"` = new instance via `create()`
- [ ] Area-specific `events.xml` limits observer to that area only

### Event Dispatch
- [ ] `$this->_eventManager->dispatch('event_name', ['key' => $value])`
- [ ] Event names are **snake_case**
- [ ] Second param is array; accessible on both `Event` and `Observer` objects
- [ ] `dispatch()` is fire-and-forget; return value is void
- [ ] AbstractModel dispatches `{prefix}_save_after` with `data_object` and `{eventObject}` keys

### Plugins vs Observers
- [ ] **Plugins** = method interception; modify args/return values; synchronous
- [ ] **Observers** = event subscription; fire-and-forget; cannot modify return values
- [ ] Use plugin when you need to change what a method receives or returns
- [ ] Use observer when you need to react to something that happened, decoupled

### Compilation & Cache
- [ ] Interceptors are generated in `generated/code/<Vendor>/<Class>/Interceptor.php`
- [ ] Must run `bin/magento setup:di:compile` after adding/changing plugins
- [ ] Must run `bin/magento cache:clean` (or `cache:flush`) after changes
- [ ] `bin/magento module:enable Vendor_Module` before `setup:upgrade`

### Common Exam Traps
- [ ] Sort order tie-breaking is **undefined** — not alphabetical by module name
- [ ] After plugins execute in **forward** sort order (same as before), not reverse
- [ ] Plugin on interface applies to DI-resolved preference, not all PHP implementations
- [ ] Global `events.xml` observer fires in ALL areas including REST API and cron
- [ ] `disabled="true"` requires matching the original `name` attribute exactly
- [ ] Both interface plugin and class plugin fire if declared — they are additive
- [ ] `type` attribute on `<plugin>` is optional in the XSD — only `name` is required
- [ ] `DataObject::getData/setData/hasData` ARE pluggable (common misconception that they aren't)

flashcards.question: What are the three types of plugins (interceptors) in Magento 2, and what can each modify?
flashcards.answer: The three types are: before (method prefix: before{MethodName}) — can modify input arguments by returning an array or return null for no change; after (prefix: after{MethodName}) — can modify the return value and must always return a value; around (prefix: around{MethodName}) — has full control over both arguments and return value via the $proceed callable. Around plugins must call $proceed() to continue the chain.
flashcards.hint: Before touches inputs, after touches outputs, and around wraps everything.

flashcards.question: What method types and class types CANNOT be intercepted by plugins in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: The following cannot be plugged: __construct and __destruct (excluded by isInterceptedMethod()), final methods and final classes, static methods (no instance context), protected and private methods (only public methods are eligible), __sleep, __wakeup, __clone, and _resetState (explicitly excluded), classes implementing NoninterceptableInterface, and classes not managed by ObjectManager.
flashcards.hint: Only public, non-final, non-static, non-constructor methods on ObjectManager-managed classes can be intercepted.

flashcards.question: How does plugin sort order affect execution, and what happens when two plugins have the same sortOrder?
flashcards.answer: Plugins execute in ascending sortOrder for all three types (before, after, and around). Lower sortOrder executes first. Around plugins nest: the outer (lower sortOrder) wraps the inner (higher sortOrder). When two plugins share the same sortOrder, the result is undefined — the framework uses uasort with no secondary sort key. The default sortOrder when omitted is 0. Always use distinct values when order matters.
flashcards.hint: Lower numbers go first, and ties are unpredictable — avoid them.

flashcards.question: What happens if an around plugin does not call $proceed()?
flashcards.answer: Not calling $proceed() silently breaks the entire plugin chain — no exception is thrown, no error is logged. All downstream plugins and the original method are skipped entirely. This is intentional by design (allowing legitimate short-circuits for caching or access control), but accidental omission is a common source of bugs. Arguments must also be forwarded with $proceed(...$args) to pass them through unmodified.
flashcards.hint: The chain breaks silently — there is no warning that downstream logic was skipped.

flashcards.question: How do you declare a plugin in di.xml, and what attributes are required?
flashcards.answer: Plugins are declared inside a <type> node using the <plugin> element. The only required attribute is 'name' (unique identifier within the type scope). Optional attributes are: 'type' (plugin class FQCN — optional, not needed when disabling), 'sortOrder' (integer, default 0), and 'disabled' (true/false, default false). You can disable a previously declared plugin using disabled='true' with the matching name without specifying the type.
flashcards.hint: Only the name is truly required — even the class is optional when you just want to disable an existing plugin.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between plugins and observers as extension mechanisms?
flashcards.answer: Plugins intercept specific method calls and can modify input arguments (before), return values (after), or both (around) — they operate synchronously on the method execution flow. Observers listen to named events dispatched via the event manager and are fire-and-forget — they cannot modify the dispatching code's return values or control flow. Use plugins to change what a method receives or returns; use observers to react to actions in a decoupled manner.
flashcards.hint: Plugins modify data flow; observers react to events without altering the flow.

flashcards.question: What interface must an observer class implement, and what is the method signature?
flashcards.answer: Observer classes must implement \Magento\Framework\Event\ObserverInterface. The only required method is execute(Observer $observer): void. Data from the dispatch is accessed via $observer->getEvent()->getData('key') or the magic getter $observer->getEvent()->getProduct(). The shortcut $observer->getData('key') also works because the data array is merged into both the Event and Observer objects.
flashcards.hint: One interface, one method, void return — observers cannot send data back to the dispatcher.

flashcards.question: How are observers registered in events.xml, and how does area scope affect them?
flashcards.answer: Observers are declared in events.xml with an <event name='...'><observer name='...' instance='...' .../></event> structure. An observer in etc/events.xml (global) fires in ALL areas including admin, frontend, REST API, and cron. An observer in etc/frontend/events.xml fires only on storefront requests. Area-specific registration limits the observer's scope. The 'shared' attribute (default true) controls whether the observer is a singleton or new instance per dispatch.
flashcards.hint: Global events.xml is like broadcasting everywhere; area-specific files narrow the audience.

flashcards.question: Why should you prefer declaring plugins on interfaces rather than concrete classes?
flashcards.answer: Plugins on interfaces apply to the class resolved via DI preference for that interface, making them more resilient to implementation changes. The interface is the contract; concrete implementations may be swapped via preference without breaking plugins. However, plugins on interfaces and concrete classes are additive — if both are declared, both fire. Interface plugins do not apply to all PHP implementations, only the one resolved through DI.
flashcards.hint: The interface is stable; the concrete class behind it may change, but your plugin still works.

flashcards.question: What does a before plugin return, and how does it affect the original method's arguments?
flashcards.answer: A before plugin returns either null (no change to arguments) or an array that replaces the positional arguments of the original method. The array maps 1-to-1 with method parameters. The first parameter of a before plugin is always $subject (the intercepted object instance), followed by the original method arguments. Returning null is the most common pattern when you only need to perform side effects before the method executes.
flashcards.hint: Null means 'pass through unchanged'; an array means 'replace all arguments with these values'.

flashcards.question: How does event dispatching work in Magento 2, and what data is available to observers?
flashcards.answer: Events are dispatched via $this->eventManager->dispatch('event_name', ['key' => $value]). The second parameter array becomes accessible on both the Event object and the Observer wrapper — dispatch() merges data into both. Data can be accessed via $observer->getEvent()->getData('key'), magic getters like $observer->getEvent()->getProduct(), or directly via $observer->getData('key'). The dispatch is fire-and-forget with a void return.
flashcards.hint: The data array is available through three equivalent access methods on the observer.

flashcards.question: How do you disable a core plugin declared by another module?
flashcards.answer: To disable a core plugin, declare a <plugin> element in your module's di.xml with the exact same 'name' attribute as the original plugin and set disabled='true'. You do not need to specify the 'type' attribute when disabling. Your module should have the original module in its <sequence> in module.xml to ensure your di.xml is merged after the original. Example: <plugin name='core_plugin_name' disabled='true'/>.
flashcards.hint: Match the plugin name exactly and set the disabled flag — no need to repeat the class reference.

flashcards.question: What is the execution order when both before, after, and around plugins are declared on the same method?
flashcards.answer: For a single plugin class with all three types: the around plugin's code before $proceed() runs, then before plugins run, then the original method, then after plugins run, then the around plugin's code after $proceed(). With multiple plugins sorted by sortOrder, around plugins nest (outer wraps inner), before plugins run in ascending order, and after plugins also run in ascending sortOrder order.
flashcards.hint: Around wraps everything like layers of an onion; before and after run inside the innermost around.

flashcards.question: What is the 'shared' attribute on an observer declaration in events.xml, and when would you set it to false?
flashcards.answer: The shared attribute (default true) controls whether the observer is instantiated as a singleton via ObjectManager::get() (shared=true) or as a new instance via ObjectManager::create() for each dispatch (shared=false). Set shared=false when the observer maintains state that should not persist between event dispatches, or when the observer processes data that must be isolated per event invocation.
flashcards.hint: It controls the same singleton vs new-instance behavior as the shared attribute on DI types.

flashcards.question: Are DataObject methods like getData(), setData(), and hasData() pluggable in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: Yes, getData(), setData(), and hasData() are real public methods on DataObject (not magic methods) and ARE pluggable. Generated interceptors include wrappers for them, and multiple core modules have plugins that intercept getData(). The commonly repeated claim that DataObject methods are not pluggable is a myth. The magic method __call() is also interceptable. Only __construct, __destruct, __sleep, __wakeup, __clone, and _resetState are excluded.
flashcards.hint: Despite common misconception, these are regular public methods fully eligible for plugin interception.

studyNotes.title: Day 8 — Caching System
studyNotes.content:
# Magento 2 Caching System — Study Notes

## Table of Contents
- [1. Overview of the Caching Architecture](#1-overview-of-the-caching-architecture)
- [2. Cache Types Reference](#2-cache-types-reference)
- [3. Cache Backends](#3-cache-backends)
- [4. Cache Invalidation Commands](#4-cache-invalidation-commands)
- [5. Programmatic Cache API](#5-programmatic-cache-api)
- [6. Custom Cache Type via cache.xml](#6-custom-cache-type-via-cachexml)
- [7. Block Cache](#7-block-cache)
- [8. Full Page Cache (FPC)](#8-full-page-cache-fpc)
- [9. Cache Tags & Tag-Based Purge](#9-cache-tags--tag-based-purge)
- [10. Tricky Exam Gotchas](#10-tricky-exam-gotchas)
- [11. Hands-On: Inspecting & Testing Cache](#11-hands-on-inspecting--testing-cache)
- [Quick-Reference Checklist](#quick-reference-checklist)

---

## 1. Overview of the Caching Architecture

Magento 2's caching system is a **layered, tag-aware** caching framework built on top of `Zend_Cache` (Laminas Cache in later versions). It provides:

- **Multiple named cache types**, each stored independently
- **Pluggable storage backends** (File, Redis, Memcached)
- **Tag-based invalidation** so only affected cache entries are purged
- **Full Page Cache (FPC)** as a first-level HTTP cache (Varnish or built-in)

```
HTTP Request
     |
     v
+--------------------+
|   Varnish / FPC    |  <-- Full Page Cache (HTTP-level)
+--------------------+
     |  MISS
     v
+--------------------+
|   Application      |
|  (PHP / Magento)   |
+--------------------+
     |
     v
+-----------------------------+
|  Block Cache  |  EAV Cache  |  Config Cache  |  etc.
+-----------------------------+
     |
     v
+--------------------+
|  Cache Backend     |  File | Redis | Memcached
+--------------------+
```

**Exam focus:**
- Understand the two-tier model: **FPC (HTTP level)** vs **application-level caches**
- Magento uses `\Magento\Framework\App\CacheInterface` as the central programmatic entry point

---

## 2. Cache Types Reference

Each cache type maps to a **unique cache ID** used in CLI commands and configuration.

| Cache ID | Name / Purpose | Invalidated When |
|---|---|---|
| `config` | Merged XML configuration | Any config XML changes |
| `layout` | XML layout handles merged per page | Layout XML file changes |
| `block_html` | Rendered HTML of cacheable blocks | Block data changes |
| `collections` | Database collection query results | Model saves/deletes |
| `reflection` | PHP class reflection metadata | New class additions |
| `db_ddl` | Database schema/DDL structure | Schema changes |
| `compiled_config` | DI-compiled configuration | `setup:di:compile` re-run |
| `eav` | EAV attribute metadata | Attribute changes |
| `customer_notification` | Customer notification flag | Notification updates |
| `full_page` | Full rendered page HTML | Content/price/stock changes |
| `translate` | Translation strings (i18n) | Translation CSV changes |
| `config_integration` | Integration OAuth tokens/config | Integration changes |
| `config_integration_api` | API access token config | Integration API changes |
| `config_webservice` | Web API config (SOAP/REST) | API config changes |

> **Note:** The exact list can vary slightly by Magento version. Run `bin/magento cache:status` on your instance to see all registered cache types.

**Exam focus:**
- `db_ddl` caches **schema structure**, not data — always flush after schema changes
- `compiled_config` is separate from `config` — it's the output of `setup:di:compile`
- `eav` caches attribute **metadata** (type, label, options), not attribute *values*
- `block_html` and `full_page` are the two caches most relevant to frontend rendering

---

## 3. Cache Backends

### 3.1 File System (Default)

- **Location:** `var/cache/` and `var/page_cache/`
- **Use case:** Development environments; zero infrastructure required
- **Performance:** Slowest of the three — I/O bound
- **Config:** Default; no `env.php` entry needed

### 3.2 Redis (Recommended for Production)

Redis is the **recommended production backend** for both application cache and session storage.

```php
// app/etc/env.php — Redis cache backend configuration
'cache' => [
    'frontend' => [
        'default' => [
            'backend' => 'Magento\\Framework\\Cache\\Backend\\Redis',
            'backend_options' => [
                'server'               => '127.0.0.1',
                'database'             => '0',
                'port'                 => '6379',
                'password'             => '',
                'compress_data'        => '1',
                'compression_lib'      => 'gzip',
            ],
        ],
        'page_cache' => [
            'backend' => 'Magento\\Framework\\Cache\\Backend\\Redis',
            'backend_options' => [
                'server'               => '127.0.0.1',
                'database'             => '1',    // Different DB from default cache
                'port'                 => '6379',
                'compress_data'        => '0',    // FPC pages usually not compressed
            ],
        ],
    ],
],
```

**Key Redis advantages:**
- In-memory: extremely fast reads/writes
- Supports **tag-based invalidation** natively via sets
- Supports persistence (`RDB` / `AOF`) for cache recovery after restart
- Separate databases (`database: 0`, `1`, etc.) to isolate cache types

**Exam focus:**
- Use **separate Redis databases** for `default` cache and `page_cache`
- Redis uses `compress_data = 1` for application cache, `0` for FPC
- Magento's Redis backend extends `Cm_Cache_Backend_Redis` (Colin Mollenhour library)

### 3.3 Memcached (Legacy)

```php
// app/etc/env.php — Memcached backend configuration
'cache' => [
    'frontend' => [
        'default' => [
            'backend' => 'Magento\\Framework\\Cache\\Backend\\Memcached',
            'backend_options' => [
                'servers' => [
                    [
                        'host'   => '127.0.0.1',
                        'port'   => 11211,
                        'weight' => 100,
                    ],
                ],
            ],
        ],
    ],
],
```

**Limitations vs Redis:**
- No native tag support — Magento emulates tags, which is slower
- No persistence — all cache lost on restart
- No built-in clustering (Redis Cluster is better supported)
- Considered **legacy** in Magento 2.x — Redis preferred

**Exam focus:**
- Memcached does **not** natively support cache tags — Magento has to simulate them
- Redis is the **recommended** production backend; Memcached is explicitly "legacy"

### 3.4 Backend Comparison Table

| Feature | File | Redis | Memcached |
|---|---|---|---|
| Performance | Low | High | High |
| Tag support | Emulated | Native | Emulated |
| Persistence | Yes (disk) | Configurable | No |
| Recommended for | Dev | Production | Legacy |
| Multi-server | No | Yes (Cluster/Sentinel) | Yes |

---

## 4. Cache Invalidation Commands

### 4.1 `cache:flush` vs `cache:clean`

This is one of the **most tested distinctions** on the exam.

```bash
# Flush: EMPTIES the entire cache storage (destroys everything including 3rd-party)
bin/magento cache:flush

# Flush specific backends
bin/magento cache:flush config layout

# Clean: Removes only INVALID/EXPIRED/TAGGED entries managed by Magento
bin/magento cache:clean

# Clean specific cache types
bin/magento cache:clean config
bin/magento cache:clean block_html full_page
```

| Command | What It Does | Scope | Safe? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cache:flush` | Calls `$backend->clean()` with `CLEANING_MODE_ALL` — empties the storage backend | ALL data in the backend, including 3rd-party caches sharing the same backend | Destructive |
| `cache:clean` | Removes entries that Magento has marked as **invalid, expired, or tag-matched** | Only Magento-managed cache entries | Safer |

**Exam focus:**
- `cache:flush` clears **ALL** cache in the storage backend — including caches from third-party extensions or external systems sharing the same Redis instance
- `cache:clean` only invalidates entries that Magento's cache framework tracks
- **Always prefer `cache:clean [type]`** when you want surgical invalidation
- `cache:flush` with no arguments flushes **every registered backend**

### 4.2 Enable / Disable Cache Types

```bash
# Check status of all cache types
bin/magento cache:status

# Enable specific types
bin/magento cache:enable full_page block_html

# Disable specific types (useful during development)
bin/magento cache:disable layout block_html
```

### 4.3 Typical Deployment Cache Sequence

```bash
# After code deployment (typical order)
bin/magento setup:upgrade              # Run schema/data patches
bin/magento setup:di:compile           # Recompile DI
bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy -f
bin/magento cache:flush                # Full flush post-deploy
```

---

## 5. Programmatic Cache API

### 5.1 `\Magento\Framework\App\CacheInterface`

The primary interface for reading and writing to the Magento cache.

```php
<?php
namespace Vendor\Module\Model;

use Magento\Framework\App\CacheInterface;
use Magento\Framework\Serialize\SerializerInterface;

class MyDataProvider
{
    private const CACHE_ID  = 'vendor_module_my_data';
    private const CACHE_TTL = 3600; // seconds

    public function __construct(
        private readonly CacheInterface      $cache,
        private readonly SerializerInterface $serializer
    ) {}

    public function getData(): array
    {
        // Attempt to load from cache
        $cached = $this->cache->load(self::CACHE_ID);

        if ($cached !== false) {
            return $this->serializer->unserialize($cached);
        }

        // Cache miss — compute the data
        $data = $this->computeExpensiveData();

        // Save with tags and TTL
        $this->cache->save(
            $this->serializer->serialize($data),
            self::CACHE_ID,
            ['vendor_module', 'my_custom_tag'],  // Cache tags
            self::CACHE_TTL
        );

        return $data;
    }

    public function invalidate(): void
    {
        // Remove a specific cache entry by ID
        $this->cache->remove(self::CACHE_ID);
    }

    private function computeExpensiveData(): array
    {
        // ... expensive DB or API call
        return ['key' => 'value'];
    }
}
```

### 5.2 CacheInterface Method Signatures

```php
// Actual interface has no PHP type hints — signatures shown here with
// docblock types for clarity.
interface CacheInterface
{
    // @return \Magento\Framework\Cache\FrontendInterface
    public function getFrontend();

    // Load cached data by ID; returns string on hit, false on miss
    // @param string $identifier
    // @return string
    public function load($identifier);

    // Save data; $tags array; $lifeTime in seconds (null = no expiry)
    // @param string $data
    // @param string $identifier
    // @param array $tags
    // @param int $lifeTime
    // @return bool
    public function save($data, $identifier, $tags = [], $lifeTime = null);

    // Remove a single entry
    // @param string $identifier
    // @return bool
    public function remove($identifier);

    // Remove ALL entries matching any of the given tags
    // @param array $tags
    // @return bool
    public function clean($tags = []);
}
```

**Exam focus:**
- `load()` returns `false` (not `null`) on a cache miss — the implementation (`Cache.php`) delegates to `FrontendInterface::load()` which returns `string|bool`
- `save()` accepts **tags as an array** — used for bulk invalidation
- `clean(array $tags)` removes all entries tagged with **any** of the given tags
- Always serialize complex data (arrays/objects) — the cache stores **strings**
- The interface also has `getFrontend()` which returns the underlying `FrontendInterface`

### 5.3 Using the Cache Type Pool

For advanced usage, you can inject specific cache frontends:

```php
use Magento\Framework\Cache\FrontendInterface;

// In di.xml — inject a specific cache frontend
```

```xml
<!-- etc/di.xml -->
<type name="Vendor\Module\Model\MyModel">
    <arguments>
        <argument name="cache" xsi:type="object">
            Magento\Framework\App\Cache\Type\Block
        </argument>
    </arguments>
</type>
```

---

## 6. Custom Cache Type via cache.xml

### 6.1 Declare the Cache Type

```xml
<!-- Vendor/Module/etc/cache.xml -->
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<config xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:Cache/etc/cache.xsd">
    <type name="vendor_module_cache"
          translate="label,description"
          instance="Vendor\Module\Cache\Type\CustomCache">
        <label>Vendor Module Cache</label>
        <description>Caches data for Vendor Module</description>
    </type>
</config>
```

### 6.2 Create the Cache Type Class

```php
<?php
namespace Vendor\Module\Cache\Type;

use Magento\Framework\App\Cache\Type\FrontendPool;
use Magento\Framework\Cache\Frontend\Decorator\TagScope;

class CustomCache extends TagScope
{
    /**
     * Cache type code — must match cache.xml 'name' attribute
     */
    public const TYPE_IDENTIFIER = 'vendor_module_cache';

    /**
     * Cache tag prefix for all entries in this cache type
     */
    public const CACHE_TAG = 'VENDOR_MODULE';

    public function __construct(FrontendPool $cacheFrontendPool)
    {
        parent::__construct(
            $cacheFrontendPool->get(self::TYPE_IDENTIFIER),
            self::CACHE_TAG
        );
    }
}
```

### 6.3 Register Cache Type in di.xml (optional but recommended)

```xml
<!-- Vendor/Module/etc/di.xml -->
<type name="Magento\Framework\App\Cache\Type\FrontendPool">
    <arguments>
        <argument name="typeCodes" xsi:type="array">
            <item name="vendor_module_cache"
                  xsi:type="string">vendor_module_cache</item>
        </argument>
    </arguments>
</type>
```

**Exam focus:**
- Custom cache types extend `TagScope` (a frontend decorator), **not** `CacheInterface`
- The `TYPE_IDENTIFIER` in the class **must match** the `name` attribute in `cache.xml`
- After adding a custom cache type, run `bin/magento cache:status` to verify it appears
- The `CACHE_TAG` constant acts as the **tag namespace** for the type

---

## 7. Block Cache

Block-level caching in Magento 2 is controlled by methods on `\Magento\Framework\View\Element\AbstractBlock`.

### 7.1 Core Block Cache Methods

```php
<?php
namespace Vendor\Module\Block;

use Magento\Framework\View\Element\Template;
use Magento\Framework\View\Element\Template\Context;

class MyBlock extends Template
{
    public function __construct(
        Context $context,
        private readonly \Magento\Customer\Model\Session $customerSession,
        array $data = []
    ) {
        parent::__construct($context, $data);
    }

    /**
     * Cache lifetime in seconds.
     * Return null  = DO NOT cache this block (default behavior).
     * Return 0     = Cache indefinitely (no expiration).
     * Return int>0 = Cache for N seconds.
     *
     * IMPORTANT: The base method is `protected`, not public.
     * It returns null by default (no caching). Override it
     * and return an integer to enable block caching.
     */
    protected function getCacheLifetime()
    {
        return 3600; // 1 hour
    }

    /**
     * The unique string key identifying this specific rendered instance.
     * If two blocks have the same key, they share the same cache entry.
     */
    public function getCacheKey(): string
    {
        return 'vendor_module_myblock_' . $this->customerSession->getCustomerGroupId();
    }

    /**
     * Array of values used to BUILD the cache key (hashed together).
     * Magento hashes these values with SHA256 to produce the final cache key string.
     * This is what most blocks should override rather than getCacheKey().
     */
    public function getCacheKeyInfo(): array
    {
        return [
            'VENDOR_MODULE_MYBLOCK',
            $this->_storeManager->getStore()->getId(),
            $this->customerSession->getCustomerGroupId(),
            $this->getTemplate(),
        ];
    }

    /**
     * Return cache tags for tag-based invalidation.
     * When a product with ID 5 changes, Magento calls
     * CacheInterface::clean(['cat_p_5']) which purges all blocks
     * that declared this tag.
     */
    public function getIdentities(): array
    {
        return [
            \Magento\Catalog\Model\Product::CACHE_TAG . '_' . $this->getProductId(),
            \Magento\Catalog\Model\Category::CACHE_TAG,
        ];
    }
}
```

### 7.2 Method Responsibilities

| Method | Return Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `getCacheLifetime()` | `int\|null` | `null` = no cache (default), `0` = indefinite, `int` = TTL seconds |
| `getCacheKey()` | `string` | Final cache key string (override for full control) |
| `getCacheKeyInfo()` | `array` | Array of values hashed to produce cache key (preferred override) |
| `getIdentities()` | `array` | Cache tags for tag-based invalidation (used for FPC too) |

**Exam focus:**
- `getCacheLifetime()` returns **`null` by default** which means **block caching is DISABLED** — you must override it and return an integer to enable caching
- `getCacheLifetime()` is **`protected`**, not public — it is called internally by `_loadCache()`
- `getCacheKeyInfo()` is the **recommended** method to override — Magento hashes the array with **SHA256** to produce the key
- `getCacheKey()` overrides the *final* key string directly — use only when you need full control
- If two different block instances return the **same `getCacheKeyInfo()`**, they share a cache entry (potentially serving wrong content)
- `getIdentities()` is used by **both block cache AND FPC** for tag-based purging

### 7.3 Block Cache in Layout XML

```xml
<!-- Layout XML — disable cache for a specific block instance -->
<block class="Vendor\Module\Block\MyBlock"
       name="vendor.my_block"
       template="Vendor_Module::my_template.phtml"
       cacheable="false" />
```

> **CRITICAL EXAM POINT:** Adding `cacheable="false"` to **any single block** on a layout handle makes the **entire page** uncacheable by FPC. This is one of the most-tested gotchas.

### 7.4 Block Cache Key Flow

```
getCacheKeyInfo() returns array
         |
         v
  array values joined with '|'
         |
         v
  SHA256 hash produced  -->  'BLOCK_' + hash = Final Cache Key
         |
         v
  Stored in block_html cache type
  with tags from getIdentities()
```

## 8. Full Page Cache (FPC)

### 8.1 FPC Backends

| Backend | Use Case | Config Location |
|---|---|---|
| **Varnish** | Production (recommended) | `app/etc/env.php` + VCL file |
| **Built-in (PHP)** | Development / staging | `Admin > Stores > Configuration > Advanced > System > Full Page Cache` |

### 8.2 Enabling Varnish

```php
// app/etc/env.php — configure Varnish as HTTP cache
'http_cache_hosts' => [
    [
        'host' => '127.0.0.1',
        'port' => '6081',   // Varnish listen port
    ],
],
```

```bash
# Generate Varnish VCL from Magento Admin
# Admin > Stores > Config > Advanced > System > Full Page Cache
# OR via CLI:
bin/magento varnish:vcl:generate \
    --export-version=6 \
    --output-file=/etc/varnish/default.vcl
```

### 8.3 ESI (Edge Side Includes) for Dynamic Blocks

ESI allows Varnish to **cache the main page** while fetching dynamic fragments separately.

```
Cached Page (Varnish)
+------------------------------------------+
|  Static content (cached 1 hour)          |
|                                          |
|  <esi:include src="/esi/cart/sidebar" /> |  <-- fetched fresh per request
|                                          |
|  Static footer (cached)                  |
+------------------------------------------+
```

ESI blocks are identified by the `ttl` data attribute. When Varnish is the FPC backend and a block has a `ttl` value set via `setTtl()`, Magento's `ProcessLayoutRenderElement` observer wraps the block output in an ESI include tag.

```php
// A block rendered via ESI must have a TTL set.
// In layout XML, use the 'ttl' argument to mark a block as ESI-eligible:
```

```xml
<!-- Layout XML — mark a block as ESI-capable with a TTL -->
<block class="Vendor\Module\Block\DynamicSidebar"
       name="vendor.dynamic.sidebar"
       template="Vendor_Module::sidebar.phtml">
    <arguments>
        <argument name="ttl" xsi:type="number">120</argument>
    </arguments>
</block>
```

**Exam focus:**
- ESI splits a page into **separately-cacheable fragments**
- Only **Varnish** supports ESI in Magento's FPC implementation — the built-in FPC does **not** support ESI
- ESI blocks are identified by having a `ttl` value (`$block->getTtl() > 0`) — this is checked by `ProcessLayoutRenderElement` observer
- Blocks with `cacheable="false"` in layout make the **entire page** non-FPC-cacheable — this is a different mechanism from ESI

### 8.4 FPC Cache Flow

```
Browser Request
      |
      v
  Varnish (checks cache)
      |
   HIT? --- YES --> Return cached response (no PHP)
      |
      NO
      |
      v
  Magento PHP Application
      |
      v
  Page rendered with X-Magento-Tags header
      |
      v
  Varnish stores response, tags it
      |
      v
  Returns to browser
```

### 8.5 Hole-Punching (Private Content)

Private/dynamic content (cart count, customer name) should **never** be in FPC. Magento handles this via:

1. **Customer sections** — loaded via JS after page loads (`/customer/section/load`)
2. **Private content blocks** — implement `\Magento\Framework\DataObject\IdentityInterface`

```php
// Private content loaded client-side — not FPC-cached
// Located in: Vendor/Module/CustomerData/MySection.php
class MySection implements \Magento\Customer\CustomerData\SectionSourceInterface
{
    public function getSectionData(): array
    {
        return ['custom_key' => $this->getPrivateData()];
    }
}
```

## 9. Cache Tags & Tag-Based Purge

### 9.1 How Cache Tags Work

Cache tags are **string labels** attached to cache entries at save time. When content changes, Magento purges all cache entries sharing a tag — without knowing which specific entries to clear.

```
Product ID 42 saved
         |
         v
Magento calls: cache:clean(['cat_p_42'])
         |
         v
ALL cache entries tagged 'cat_p_42' are invalidated:
  - block_html entries for product pages
  - FPC entries for PDPs showing product 42
  - Any custom cache entries tagged 'cat_p_42'
```

### 9.2 Standard Magento Cache Tags

```php
// Common cache tag constants
\Magento\Catalog\Model\Product::CACHE_TAG          // 'cat_p'
\Magento\Catalog\Model\Category::CACHE_TAG         // 'cat_c'
\Magento\Cms\Model\Page::CACHE_TAG                 // 'cms_p'
\Magento\Cms\Model\Block::CACHE_TAG                // 'cms_b'
\Magento\Catalog\Model\Product\Type\Price::CACHE_TAG // 'PRODUCT_PRICE'

// Tag with specific entity ID
$tags = [\Magento\Catalog\Model\Product::CACHE_TAG . '_' . $productId];
// Result: 'cat_p_42'
```

### 9.3 X-Magento-Tags HTTP Header

When Varnish is active, Magento sends cache tags in an HTTP header that Varnish reads to associate the response with those tags.

```
HTTP Response Headers (Magento -> Varnish)
----------------------------------------------
X-Magento-Tags: cat_p_42,cat_c_5,cms_b_3,FPC
Cache-Control: max-age=86400, public, s-maxage=86400
```

```
HTTP Request (Admin save triggers purge -> Varnish)
----------------------------------------------
PURGE / HTTP/1.1
X-Magento-Tags-Pattern: cat_p_42
```

**Exam focus:**
- `X-Magento-Tags` header carries the tags for Varnish to store
- When content is updated in Admin, Magento sends a **BAN/PURGE** request to Varnish with the affected tags
- The VCL file must be configured to handle these purge requests
- Tags accumulate — a product page may have `cat_p_42,cat_c_5,store_1` etc.

### 9.4 IdentityInterface

Blocks and models that produce cacheable content should implement `IdentityInterface`:

```php
<?php
namespace Vendor\Module\Block;

use Magento\Framework\DataObject\IdentityInterface;
use Magento\Framework\View\Element\Template;

class ProductInfoBlock extends Template implements IdentityInterface
{
    /**
     * Must return array of cache tags.
     * Called by FPC to determine X-Magento-Tags for the response.
     */
    public function getIdentities(): array
    {
        $identities = [];

        if ($product = $this->getProduct()) {
            // Tag for the specific product
            $identities[] = \Magento\Catalog\Model\Product::CACHE_TAG
                . '_' . $product->getId();

            // Tag for all products (broad invalidation)
            $identities[] = \Magento\Catalog\Model\Product::CACHE_TAG;
        }

        return $identities;
    }
}
```

## 10. Tricky Exam Gotchas

### 10.1 `cache:flush` vs `cache:clean` (The Big One)

```
cache:flush
-----------
- Calls $backend->clean() with CLEANING_MODE_ALL
- Removes EVERYTHING in the storage backend
- Affects third-party data sharing the same backend
- Dispatches 'adminhtml_cache_flush_all' event for full_page
- Analogy: "Format the hard drive"

cache:clean
-----------
- Removes only Magento-managed, invalid/expired entries
- Respects cache type boundaries, also clears invalidation tracker
- Does NOT affect third-party data
- Can be scoped: bin/magento cache:clean config layout
- Dispatches 'adminhtml_cache_flush_system' event
- Analogy: "Empty the recycling bin"
```

**Exam focus:** `cache:flush` can destroy cached data from **other applications** sharing the same Redis instance. Always use `cache:clean` for targeted invalidation in production.

### 10.2 `cacheable="false"` Poisons the Entire Page

```xml
<!-- This ONE declaration makes the ENTIRE page non-FPC-cacheable -->
<block class="Vendor\Module\Block\DynamicBlock"
       name="my.dynamic.block"
       cacheable="false" />
```

```
Page Layout Processing
         |
         v
  Any block with cacheable="false" found?
         |
        YES
         |
         v
  Entire page response: Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store
         |
         v
  Varnish/FPC: NEVER caches this page
  (Even if 99% of content is static)
```

**Exam focus:**
- `cacheable="false"` on **any single block** in the layout = **entire page uncacheable**
- This is checked by `Layout::isCacheable()` which uses XPath to find any block with `cacheable="false"`
- This is a common performance bug in production — audit third-party modules for this
- Solution: use **private content sections** (JS-loaded) or **ESI** instead

### 10.3 Block Cache Key Collisions

```php
// BAD: Two instances that should be different share the same cache key
public function getCacheKeyInfo(): array
{
    return ['MY_BLOCK']; // No differentiators!
}

// GOOD: Differentiate by store, customer group, template, and custom data
public function getCacheKeyInfo(): array
{
    return [
        'MY_BLOCK',
        $this->_storeManager->getStore()->getId(),
        $this->customerSession->getCustomerGroupId(),
        $this->getTemplate(),
        $this->getData('my_custom_param'),
    ];
}
```

**Exam focus:** Identical `getCacheKeyInfo()` arrays = shared cache entry = potentially wrong cached content served to different users.

### 10.4 Serialization Requirement

```php
// WRONG — arrays cannot be stored directly
$this->cache->save($arrayData, 'my_id');

// CORRECT — serialize first
$this->cache->save(
    $this->serializer->serialize($arrayData),
    'my_id'
);
// And when loading:
$data = $this->serializer->unserialize($this->cache->load('my_id'));
```

### 10.5 Cache Disabled != Cache Flushed

```bash
bin/magento cache:disable full_page
# The cache TYPE is disabled (Magento won't write/read it)
# BUT existing entries are still in storage

bin/magento cache:enable full_page
# Re-enabling reads OLD stale entries if not flushed
# Always flush after re-enabling if data may be stale
```

### 10.6 `compiled_config` vs `config`

| Cache Type | What It Caches | When to Clear |
|---|---|---|
| `config` | Merged XML configuration (`config.xml`, `system.xml`, etc.) | After changing any `etc/*.xml` config files |
| `compiled_config` | Output of `setup:di:compile` (DI preferences, interceptors, etc.) | After `setup:di:compile` or class changes |

### 10.7 `getCacheLifetime()` Returns `null` by Default

```php
// WRONG assumption: "null means cached forever"
// null actually means BLOCK CACHING IS DISABLED.
// The _loadCache() method skips caching entirely when getCacheLifetime() === null.

// To cache indefinitely (no TTL expiration):
protected function getCacheLifetime()
{
    return 0; // 0 = cache with no expiration
}

// To cache for a specific duration:
protected function getCacheLifetime()
{
    return 3600; // 1 hour
}

// To NOT cache (default behavior — no override needed):
// Just don't override getCacheLifetime() at all; it returns null.
```

### 11.2 Test Block Cache Invalidation via `getIdentities()`

**Step 1: Create a block that caches product data**

```php
<?php
// Vendor/Module/Block/ProductInfo.php
namespace Vendor\Module\Block;

use Magento\Catalog\Api\ProductRepositoryInterface;
use Magento\Framework\DataObject\IdentityInterface;
use Magento\Framework\View\Element\Template;
use Magento\Framework\View\Element\Template\Context;

class ProductInfo extends Template implements IdentityInterface
{
    public function __construct(
        Context $context,
        private readonly ProductRepositoryInterface $productRepository,
        array $data = []
    ) {
        parent::__construct($context, $data);
    }

    public function getProduct(): ?\Magento\Catalog\Api\Data\ProductInterface
    {
        $productId = $this->getData('product_id');
        if (!$productId) {
            return null;
        }
        return $this->productRepository->getById($productId);
    }

    // Block cache TTL — protected, not public
    protected function getCacheLifetime()
    {
        return 3600;
    }

    // Cache key includes product ID and store
    public function getCacheKeyInfo(): array
    {
        return [
            'VENDOR_PRODUCT_INFO',
            $this->getData('product_id'),
            $this->_storeManager->getStore()->getId(),
        ];
    }

    // Tags for invalidation
    public function getIdentities(): array
    {
        $product = $this->getProduct();
        if (!$product) {
            return [];
        }

        return [
            \Magento\Catalog\Model\Product::CACHE_TAG . '_' . $product->getId(),
        ];
    }
}
```

**Step 2: Add block to layout**

```xml
<!-- Vendor/Module/view/frontend/layout/catalog_product_view.xml -->
<page xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
      xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:View/Layout/etc/page_configuration.xsd">
    <body>
        <referenceContainer name="content">
            <block class="Vendor\Module\Block\ProductInfo"
                   name="vendor.product.info"
                   template="Vendor_Module::product_info.phtml">
                <arguments>
                    <argument name="product_id" xsi:type="string">42</argument>
                </arguments>
            </block>
        </referenceContainer>
    </body>
</page>
```

**Step 3: Verify invalidation**

```bash
# 1. Load the product page — block is rendered and cached
curl -s http://magento.local/catalog/product/view/id/42 > /dev/null

# 2. Check Redis to see cached entries (if using Redis)
redis-cli -n 0 keys "*VENDOR_PRODUCT_INFO*"

# 3. Save the product in Admin (triggers identity invalidation)
# Magento calls: $this->cache->clean(['cat_p_42'])

# 4. Load page again — block should be re-rendered from fresh data
# (cache miss for the block, new entry stored)

# 5. Manually clean by tag
bin/magento cache:clean block_html
# OR programmatically clean specific tag:
# $this->cache->clean([\Magento\Catalog\Model\Product::CACHE_TAG . '_42']);
```

### 11.3 Verifying FPC Headers

```bash
# Check if Varnish/FPC is caching a page
curl -I http://magento.local/

# Look for these headers:
# X-Cache: HIT          <- Varnish served from cache
# X-Cache: MISS         <- Varnish fetched from backend
# X-Magento-Tags: ...   <- Only present on first request (stripped after caching)
# Age: 3600             <- Seconds the response has been in Varnish cache

# Check if a page is NOT cached (cacheable="false" present):
# Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate
# Pragma: no-cache
```

## Quick-Reference Checklist

### Cache Types
- [ ] 14 built-in cache types: `config`, `layout`, `block_html`, `collections`, `reflection`, `db_ddl`, `compiled_config`, `eav`, `customer_notification`, `full_page`, `translate`, `config_integration`, `config_integration_api`, `config_webservice`
- [ ] `db_ddl` = database **schema** structure (not data)
- [ ] `compiled_config` = output of `setup:di:compile` (distinct from `config`)
- [ ] `eav` = EAV attribute **metadata** only

### Cache Backends
- [ ] **File** = default, development, slowest
- [ ] **Redis** = recommended for production, native tag support, in-memory
- [ ] **Memcached** = legacy, no native tag support, no persistence
- [ ] Redis uses separate **databases** for `default` vs `page_cache`
- [ ] `compress_data = 1` for application cache; `0` for FPC in Redis

### Cache Invalidation Commands
- [ ] `cache:flush` = **empties entire storage backend** including third-party data
- [ ] `cache:clean [type]` = removes only Magento-managed invalid/expired entries
- [ ] `cache:flush` is destructive; `cache:clean` is surgical
- [ ] `cache:status` = shows enabled/disabled state of all types
- [ ] `cache:enable` / `cache:disable` = toggles types without clearing data

### Programmatic Cache
- [ ] Use `\Magento\Framework\App\CacheInterface` for read/write
- [ ] `load()` returns `false` (not `null`) on cache miss
- [ ] `save($data, $id, $tags, $lifeTime)` — data must be a **string** (serialize arrays)
- [ ] `clean(array $tags)` purges all entries with **any** of the given tags
- [ ] Always use `SerializerInterface` to serialize/unserialize complex data

### Custom Cache Type
- [ ] Declare in `etc/cache.xml` with `name`, `instance`, `label`, `description`
- [ ] Class extends `TagScope` (not `CacheInterface`)
- [ ] `TYPE_IDENTIFIER` constant must match `name` in `cache.xml`
- [ ] `CACHE_TAG` constant is the tag namespace for the type

### Block Cache
- [ ] `getCacheLifetime()`: **`null` = NO CACHE (default)**, `0` = indefinite, `int` = TTL seconds
- [ ] `getCacheLifetime()` is **`protected`**, not public
- [ ] `getCacheKeyInfo()` = array hashed with **SHA256** to produce key (preferred to override)
- [ ] `getCacheKey()` = final key string (override for full control)
- [ ] `getIdentities()` = cache tags for invalidation (used by block cache AND FPC)
- [ ] Same `getCacheKeyInfo()` result = shared cache entry = potential wrong content served

### Full Page Cache
- [ ] **Varnish** = production FPC; **built-in PHP** = development FPC
- [ ] **ESI** = Varnish-only; blocks with `getTtl() > 0` are wrapped in ESI includes
- [ ] `cacheable="false"` on **one block** = **entire page** becomes uncacheable
- [ ] Private content (cart, customer name) loaded client-side via `/customer/section/load`
- [ ] `IdentityInterface::getIdentities()` provides tags for FPC tag-based purging

### Cache Tags & X-Magento-Tags
- [ ] `X-Magento-Tags` HTTP header carries tags Varnish uses to store/purge responses
- [ ] Magento sends PURGE/BAN requests to Varnish when content is saved in Admin
- [ ] Standard tags: `cat_p`, `cat_c`, `cms_p`, `cms_b` (often suffixed with `_ID`)
- [ ] Tag format: `CACHE_TAG_CONSTANT . '_' . $entityId` (e.g., `cat_p_42`)
- [ ] VCL file must be generated and configured to handle purge requests
- [ ] `Price::CACHE_TAG` is `'PRODUCT_PRICE'` (not `cat_p_price`)

### Critical Gotchas
- [ ] `cache:flush` nukes **all** data in the backend — use with caution in production
- [ ] `cacheable="false"` on ANY block disables FPC for the **entire page**
- [ ] `cache:disable` does NOT flush — stale data remains and is served after re-enable
- [ ] `compiled_config` != `config` — they cache different things
- [ ] Memcached has **no native tag support** — Magento emulates it (slower)
- [ ] ESI is **Varnish-only** — built-in FPC does not support ESI
- [ ] Missing `getCacheKeyInfo()` differentiators = block cache key collisions
- [ ] `getCacheLifetime()` default `null` = **not cached**, NOT "cached forever"

flashcards.question: How do you create a custom cache type in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: Declare the cache type in `etc/cache.xml` with a `name`, `instance`, `label`, and `description`. Create a PHP class that extends `TagScope` (not `CacheInterface`), with a `TYPE_IDENTIFIER` constant matching the `name` in cache.xml and a `CACHE_TAG` constant as the tag namespace. The constructor calls `parent::__construct()` with the FrontendPool and cache tag.
flashcards.hint: The declaration file is specific to caching, and the class extends a frontend decorator, not the main cache interface.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between `cache:flush` and `cache:clean` in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: `cache:flush` calls the backend's `clean()` with CLEANING_MODE_ALL, which empties the entire storage backend including third-party data sharing the same Redis instance. `cache:clean` removes only Magento-managed entries that are invalid, expired, or tag-matched. Always prefer `cache:clean [type]` for targeted invalidation in production.
flashcards.hint: One is like formatting the hard drive, the other is like emptying the recycling bin.

flashcards.question: What does `getCacheLifetime()` return by default on a block, and what does each possible return value mean?
flashcards.answer: By default, `getCacheLifetime()` returns `null`, which means block caching is DISABLED entirely. Returning `0` means the block is cached indefinitely with no expiration. Returning a positive integer (e.g., 3600) caches the block for that many seconds. This is a protected method, not public.
flashcards.hint: The default return value is often mistaken for 'cached forever' but it's actually the opposite.

flashcards.question: What happens when any single block in a layout has the attribute `cacheable="false"`?
flashcards.answer: Adding `cacheable="false"` to any single block in a page's layout makes the ENTIRE page uncacheable by Full Page Cache. Magento's `Layout::isCacheable()` uses XPath to find any block with this attribute, and if found, sets Cache-Control to no-cache/no-store. This is a common performance bug caused by third-party modules.
flashcards.hint: One bad apple spoils the entire barrel — the scope of impact is broader than just that block.

flashcards.question: Which cache backend is recommended for Magento 2 production, and why is it preferred over Memcached?
flashcards.answer: Redis is the recommended production backend. It provides native tag-based invalidation via sets, configurable persistence (RDB/AOF), supports separate databases for default cache and page_cache, and offers multi-server support via Redis Cluster/Sentinel. Memcached lacks native tag support (Magento must emulate it), has no persistence, and is considered legacy.
flashcards.hint: This in-memory data store supports native tag operations and database separation.

flashcards.question: What is the role of `getIdentities()` in Magento 2 block caching, and where is it used?
flashcards.answer: `getIdentities()` returns an array of cache tags used for tag-based invalidation. It is used by both the block cache (block_html) and Full Page Cache for purging. When a product is saved, Magento purges all cache entries sharing that product's tag (e.g., `cat_p_42`). Blocks implementing `IdentityInterface` must define this method.
flashcards.hint: This method provides the tag strings that connect content changes to cache purging — used at both block and HTTP cache levels.

flashcards.question: How does Magento 2 communicate cache tags to Varnish for FPC, and how does purging work?
flashcards.answer: Magento sends cache tags via the `X-Magento-Tags` HTTP response header (e.g., `cat_p_42,cat_c_5,cms_b_3,FPC`). Varnish reads these tags and associates them with the cached response. When content changes in Admin, Magento sends a PURGE/BAN request to Varnish with an `X-Magento-Tags-Pattern` header containing the affected tags.
flashcards.hint: Tags travel from Magento to Varnish via a specific HTTP header, and purge requests flow back the other direction.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between `getCacheKey()` and `getCacheKeyInfo()` on a Magento 2 block?
flashcards.answer: `getCacheKeyInfo()` returns an array of values that Magento hashes with SHA256 to produce the final cache key — this is the recommended method to override. `getCacheKey()` returns the final cache key string directly, giving full control. If two block instances return identical `getCacheKeyInfo()` arrays, they share a cache entry and may serve wrong content.
flashcards.hint: One returns raw ingredients that get hashed; the other returns the finished product directly.

flashcards.question: What does `CacheInterface::load()` return on a cache miss, and what data type does `save()` accept?
flashcards.answer: `load()` returns `false` (not `null`) on a cache miss. `save()` accepts a string as data — arrays and objects must be serialized first using `SerializerInterface`. The full signature is `save($data, $identifier, $tags = [], $lifeTime = null)` where tags enable bulk invalidation.
flashcards.hint: The miss value is a boolean, not a null. The storage format is always the simplest string type.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between the `config` and `compiled_config` cache types?
flashcards.answer: The `config` cache stores merged XML configuration from `config.xml`, `system.xml`, and other XML config files. The `compiled_config` cache stores the output of `setup:di:compile` including DI preferences, interceptors, and generated code. They cache fundamentally different things and should be cleared at different times.
flashcards.hint: One caches XML merging results, the other caches dependency injection compilation output.

flashcards.question: What does ESI (Edge Side Includes) do in Magento's FPC implementation, and which backend supports it?
flashcards.answer: ESI allows Varnish to cache the main page while fetching dynamic fragments separately per request. Only Varnish supports ESI — the built-in PHP FPC does not. ESI blocks are identified by having a `ttl` value set (checked via `$block->getTtl() > 0`), and Magento's `ProcessLayoutRenderElement` observer wraps them in ESI include tags.
flashcards.hint: This technique splits a page into separately-cacheable fragments, but only works with the external HTTP cache.

flashcards.question: Why is it important to use separate Redis databases for `default` cache and `page_cache` in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: Separate Redis databases (e.g., database 0 for default cache and database 1 for page_cache) isolate cache types from each other. This prevents a `cache:flush` on one type from accidentally clearing the other. Redis configuration also differs: `compress_data = 1` is typically used for application cache while `compress_data = 0` is used for FPC.
flashcards.hint: Isolation prevents one flush operation from impacting the other type, and compression settings differ between them.

flashcards.question: How does Magento handle private/dynamic content (like cart count and customer name) in a Full Page Cache environment?
flashcards.answer: Private content is never stored in FPC. Magento uses customer sections loaded via JavaScript after the page loads, making an AJAX call to `/customer/section/load`. Private content blocks implement `SectionSourceInterface` and return data that is fetched client-side, ensuring the cached page remains generic while dynamic data is personalized per user.
flashcards.hint: The solution involves loading personalized data asynchronously after the cached page is served.

flashcards.question: What happens if you disable a cache type with `cache:disable` and then re-enable it?
flashcards.answer: Disabling a cache type stops Magento from reading/writing that cache type, but existing entries remain in storage. When you re-enable it, Magento reads those old stale entries. You should always flush or clean the cache type after re-enabling to avoid serving stale data.
flashcards.hint: Disabling doesn't clear — it only stops access. The stale data is still sitting there waiting.

flashcards.question: What does the `db_ddl` cache type store in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: The `db_ddl` cache stores database schema (DDL) structure — table definitions, column types, and indexes. It does NOT cache actual data. This cache should always be flushed after schema changes such as adding columns or running `setup:upgrade`. It is one of the 14 built-in cache types.
flashcards.hint: Think of it as caching the 'blueprint' of the database, not the contents.

studyNotes.title: Day 9 — Stores, Websites & Store Views
studyNotes.content:
# Magento 2 Stores, Websites & Store Views — Study Notes

## Table of Contents
- [1. Overview: The Three-Tier Hierarchy](#1-overview-the-three-tier-hierarchy)
- [2. Websites](#2-websites)
- [3. Stores (Store Groups)](#3-stores-store-groups)
- [4. Store Views](#4-store-views)
- [5. Configuration Scope & Inheritance](#5-configuration-scope--inheritance)
- [6. Customer Accounts & Scope](#6-customer-accounts--scope)
- [7. Product Catalog & Scope](#7-product-catalog--scope)
- [8. URL Configuration Per Store View](#8-url-configuration-per-store-view)
- [9. Multi-Store Setup Patterns](#9-multi-store-setup-patterns)
- [10. Admin Navigation & Setup](#10-admin-navigation--setup)
- [11. Common Tricky Exam Scenarios](#11-common-tricky-exam-scenarios)
- [12. Quick-Reference Checklist](#12-quick-reference-checklist)

---

## 1. Overview: The Three-Tier Hierarchy

Magento 2 organises all commerce content using a **three-tier scope model**. Understanding exactly *what lives at which level* is the most-tested topic in this section.

```
+--------------------------------------------------+
|               GLOBAL / DEFAULT                   |
|  (fallback for everything not overridden below)  |
|                                                  |
|  +--------------------------------------------+ |
|  |              WEBSITE (Brand / Country)     | |
|  |  - Customer accounts                       | |
|  |  - Product visibility                      | |
|  |  - Shared payment / shipping config        | |
|  |                                            | |
|  |  +--------------------------------------+  | |
|  |  |    STORE / STORE GROUP               |  | |
|  |  |    (Category Structure)              |  | |
|  |  |  - Root category assignment          |  | |
|  |  |  - One default store view required   |  | |
|  |  |                                      |  | |
|  |  |  +--------------------------------+  |  | |
|  |  |  |  STORE VIEW (Language/Locale)  |  |  | |
|  |  |  |  - Display language            |  |  | |
|  |  |  |  - Locale / currency display   |  |  | |
|  |  |  |  - Base URLs                   |  |  | |
|  |  |  |  - Translated content          |  |  | |
|  |  |  +--------------------------------+  |  | |
|  |  +--------------------------------------+  | |
|  +--------------------------------------------+ |
+--------------------------------------------------+
```

| Tier | Also Called | Primary Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| **Website** | Website | Brand, country, customer base separation |
| **Store** | Store Group | Root category (product navigation tree) |
| **Store View** | Store View | Language, locale, translated content |

> **Exam focus:** The "Store" in Magento 2 is technically a **Store Group** — it is NOT a store view. Candidates frequently confuse Store with Store View.

---

## 2. Websites

### What a Website Controls
- **Customer accounts** — customers register *to a specific website*; their account does not carry over to another website by default
- **Payment methods** — can be configured per website
- **Shipping methods** — can be configured per website
- **Product visibility** — products are *assigned to websites*, not to store views

### Creating a Website (Admin Path)
```
Stores > Settings > All Stores > Create Website
```

### Database Representation
```sql
-- Core website table
SELECT website_id, code, name, sort_order, default_group_id, is_default
FROM store_website;
```

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `website_id` | Auto-increment PK (smallint unsigned) |
| `code` | Unique string code (varchar(32), used in code/config) |
| `name` | Human-readable label (varchar(64)) |
| `sort_order` | Display order (smallint unsigned, default 0) |
| `default_group_id` | FK to the default store (group) for this website |
| `is_default` | Only one website can be the admin default (smallint, default 0) |

> **Exam focus:** A **website** is the *highest* customer-facing scope. Customer accounts are scoped to the website, not globally (unless the "Share Customer Accounts" setting is changed).

---

## 3. Stores (Store Groups)

### What a Store Controls
- **Root Category assignment** — each store has exactly **one root category**; this determines the entire navigation tree visible on the frontend
- Acts as the container for one or more store views
- **One store view must be designated as the default** for the store

### Root Category Relationship

```
Website A
  |
  +-- Store: "Main Store"  (Root Category: "Default Category")
  |     |
  |     +-- Store View: English
  |     +-- Store View: French
  |
  +-- Store: "Outlet Store" (Root Category: "Outlet Category")
        |
        +-- Store View: English Outlet
```

### Database Representation
```sql
-- store_group table
SELECT group_id, website_id, name, root_category_id, default_store_id, code
FROM store_group;
```

> **Exam focus:** Switching the **root category** on a store changes which products/categories appear in navigation. Two stores under the same website share customer accounts but can have completely different navigation trees.

> **Exam focus:** A store (group) must have **at least one store view** to be functional. A store view marked as the default is used when no specific store view is requested.

---

## 4. Store Views

### What a Store View Controls
- **Display language / locale** (e.g., `en_US`, `fr_FR`, `de_DE`)
- **Currency display** (not the base currency — that is website-level)
- **Base URL** (each store view can have its own domain or path)
- **Translated product attributes** (name, description per store view)
- **Static blocks / CMS content** per view

### Creating a Store View (Admin Path)
```
Stores > Settings > All Stores > Create Store View
```

### Key Store View Fields
| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `Store` | Which store (group) this view belongs to |
| `Name` | Label shown in the store switcher |
| `Code` | Unique string (used in URL if store codes enabled) |
| `Is Active` | Enabled / Disabled (column name is `is_active`, not `status`) |
| `Sort Order` | Position in store switcher |

```sql
-- Core store view table (named "store" in the DB)
SELECT store_id, code, website_id, group_id, name, sort_order, is_active
FROM store;
```

> **Exam focus:** `store_id = 0` is the **Admin store**. `store_id = 1` is conventionally the first default store view, but this is not guaranteed. The column is `is_active` (not `status`).

---

## 5. Configuration Scope & Inheritance

### The Inheritance Chain

Configuration in Magento has **three** levels (not four). Store Group is **not** a configuration scope — it is a structural entity for grouping store views and assigning root categories.

```
DEFAULT (Global)
    |
    v  (overrides Default for this Website)
WEBSITE
    |
    v  (overrides Website for this Store View)
STORE VIEW
```

Values cascade **downward**. If no override exists at a lower level, Magento uses the value from the next level up. The `core_config_data` table only stores three scope values: `'default'`, `'website'`, and `'store'` (which means store view).

### "Use Default" / "Use Website" Checkbox

When you configure a setting at Website or Store View scope, you will see an **inheritance checkbox** next to each field.

- At **Website scope** the checkbox says **"Use Default"** — check it to inherit from Default
- At **Store View scope** the checkbox says **"Use Website"** (when the field supports website scope) — check it to inherit from the Website above

```
+----------------------------------+
|  Configuration Field: Tax Class  |
```
