```
|  [x] Use Default   Value: ---    |  <-- Website scope: inherits from Default
|  [ ] Use Default   Value: VAT    |  <-- Website scope: overrides Default
+----------------------------------+
|  [x] Use Website   Value: ---    |  <-- Store View: inherits from Website
|  [ ] Use Website   Value: ""     |  <-- Store View: explicit blank override
+----------------------------------+
```

> **Exam focus:** Unchecking the inheritance checkbox and saving a blank value is NOT the same as checking it. A blank explicit value overrides (with blank) rather than inheriting.

### Scope in `config.xml` / `system.xml`

Developers declare the *maximum* allowed scope for each configuration path:

```xml
<!-- In system.xml -->
<field id="my_setting" type="text" sortOrder="10" showInDefault="1"
       showInWebsite="1" showInStore="1">
    <label>My Setting</label>
</field>
```

| Attribute | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `showInDefault="1"` | Visible/editable at Default scope |
| `showInWebsite="1"` | Visible/editable at Website scope |
| `showInStore="1"` | Visible/editable at **Store View** scope (confusingly named) |

### Retrieving Scoped Config in Code

```php
<?php
// app/code/Vendor/Module/Model/Example.php

use Magento\Framework\App\Config\ScopeConfigInterface;
use Magento\Store\Model\ScopeInterface;

class Example
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly ScopeConfigInterface $scopeConfig
    ) {}

    public function getSetting(): string
    {
        // Retrieve for current store view
        return $this->scopeConfig->getValue(
            'vendor_module/general/my_setting',
            ScopeInterface::SCOPE_STORE   // 'store' = store view scope
        );
    }

    public function getSettingForWebsite(int $websiteId): string
    {
        return $this->scopeConfig->getValue(
            'vendor_module/general/my_setting',
            ScopeInterface::SCOPE_WEBSITE,
            $websiteId
        );
    }
}
```

> **Exam focus:** `ScopeInterface::SCOPE_STORE` refers to **store view** scope (confusingly named). `SCOPE_WEBSITE` is website scope.

### Scope Constants Quick Reference

```php
<?php
// Magento\Store\Model\ScopeInterface — 6 constants total
const SCOPE_STORES   = 'stores';   // plural — used in config.php paths
const SCOPE_GROUPS   = 'groups';   // plural — store group scope
const SCOPE_WEBSITES = 'websites'; // plural
const SCOPE_STORE    = 'store';    // singular — used in getValue()
const SCOPE_GROUP    = 'group';    // Store group scope
const SCOPE_WEBSITE  = 'website';  // singular — used in getValue()
```

---

## 6. Customer Accounts & Scope

### Default Behaviour: Per Website

```
Website A                    Website B
  |                            |
  +-- Customer: john@ex.com    +-- Customer: john@ex.com
  |   (account #1)             |   (account #2, SEPARATE)
  |                            |
  +-- Store View: EN           +-- Store View: EN
  +-- Store View: FR
```

- By default, the same email address can be registered on **both** websites as separate accounts
- Orders, addresses, and wish-lists are all scoped to the website's customer account

### Sharing Customer Accounts

The behaviour can be changed at:
```
Stores > Configuration > Customers > Customer Configuration > Account Sharing Options
```

| Option | Value | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| **Per Website** | `1` | *(Default)* Separate accounts per website |
| **Global** | `0` | One customer account works across all websites |

> **Exam focus:** The exam frequently tests that customer accounts are **per Website by default**, NOT per store or store view. Changing to "Global" sharing is a deliberate configuration choice. The default value in `config.xml` is `1` (SHARE_WEBSITE).

### Database Impact

```sql
-- customer_entity table — website_id column scopes the customer
SELECT entity_id, email, website_id
FROM customer_entity
WHERE email = 'john@example.com';
-- May return multiple rows (one per website)

-- Unique constraint is on (email, website_id), allowing the same email on different websites
```

---

## 7. Product Catalog & Scope

### Product-to-Website Assignment

Products are **assigned to Websites**, not to store views.

```
Product: "Blue Widget"
  |
  +-- Assigned to: Website A   (visible in all stores/views under Website A)
  +-- Assigned to: Website B   (also visible under Website B)
  |
  NOT assigned per: Store Group, Store View
```

**Admin path to assign product to website:**
```
Catalog > Products > Edit Product > Product in Websites (tab)
```

> **Exam focus:** This is a common exam trap. You **cannot** assign a product to a specific store view — you assign it to a website, and it becomes visible to all store views under that website.

### Product Attributes & Store View Scope

While product-to-website assignment is at website level, **attribute values** (name, description, etc.) can be scoped to store view level:

```
Product: "Blue Widget"
  |
  +-- Name (Default):          "Blue Widget"
  +-- Name (Store View: FR):   "Widget Bleu"
  +-- Description (Default):   "A quality widget."
  +-- Description (Store View: FR): "Un widget de qualité."
```

### Attribute Scope Settings

```
Stores > Attributes > Product > [Edit Attribute] > Scope
```

| Scope | EAV Constant | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Store View** | `SCOPE_STORE` | `0` | Value can differ per store view |
| **Global** | `SCOPE_GLOBAL` | `1` | Single value across all websites |
| **Website** | `SCOPE_WEBSITE` | `2` | Value shared across all store views in a website |

> **Exam focus:** The `price` attribute is **Global** scope by default (set by data patch `ChangePriceAttributeDefaultScope` which overrides the initial SCOPE_WEBSITE definition in CategorySetup). The `name` and `description` attributes are **Store View** scope (SCOPE_STORE = 0) by default. Changing price scope to Website allows different prices per website. Note the confusing naming: `ScopedAttributeInterface::SCOPE_STORE` = store **view** scope.

### Root Category & Store-Level Visibility

Even though products are assigned to websites, the **navigation visibility** is filtered through the store's root category:

```
Website A
  +-- Store: "Main Store"  (Root: Default Category)
  |     Products in "Default Category" tree appear in nav
  |
  +-- Store: "Outlet"  (Root: Outlet Category)
        Only products in "Outlet Category" tree appear in nav
        (even if product is assigned to Website A)
```

---

## 8. URL Configuration Per Store View

### Base URL Settings (Per Store View)

```
Stores > Configuration > General > Web > Base URLs
```

| Setting | Example Value | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Base URL | `https://www.example.com/` | HTTP base URL for this store view |
| Base URL (Secure) | `https://www.example.com/` | HTTPS base URL |
| Base Link URL | `{{unsecure_base_url}}` | Dynamic reference |

### Multi-Domain Setup (One Domain Per Website)

```
Website A:  https://www.brand-a.com/
Website B:  https://www.brand-b.com/
```

Each store view under Website A and B gets its own base URL configured in Admin.

### Subdirectory / Store Code Approach

Instead of separate domains, store codes can be embedded in URLs:

```
https://www.example.com/          <- Default store view
https://www.example.com/fr/       <- French store view (code: fr)
https://www.example.com/de/       <- German store view (code: de)
```

**Enable store code in URL:**
```
Stores > Configuration > General > Web > Url Options
  > Add Store Code to Urls = Yes
```

> **Exam focus:** When "Add Store Code to URLs" is enabled, Magento appends the store view code to the URL path. This is one approach to multi-language; the other is separate base URLs (subdomains or domains).

### `.htaccess` / `nginx` Store Switching

With Apache, the `MAGE_RUN_CODE` and `MAGE_RUN_TYPE` environment variables can force a specific store/website:

```apache
# .htaccess or VirtualHost
SetEnvIf Host "brand-a\.com" MAGE_RUN_CODE=base
SetEnvIf Host "brand-a\.com" MAGE_RUN_TYPE=website

SetEnvIf Host "brand-b\.com" MAGE_RUN_CODE=brand_b_website
SetEnvIf Host "brand-b\.com" MAGE_RUN_TYPE=website
```

```nginx
# nginx server block
server {
    server_name brand-b.com;
    fastcgi_param MAGE_RUN_CODE brand_b_website;
    fastcgi_param MAGE_RUN_TYPE website;
}
```

> **Exam focus:** `MAGE_RUN_TYPE` accepts three values: `website`, `store` (store view), or `group` (store group). The values come from `StoreResolver\ReaderList` which maps each to a resolver class. Most commonly you'll use `website` or `store`.

---

## 9. Multi-Store Setup Patterns

### Pattern 1: Website Per Brand/Country

```
+-------------------+      +-------------------+
|   Website: US     |      |   Website: EU     |
|   brand.com       |      |   brand.eu        |
|                   |      |                   |
| Store: Main       |      | Store: Main       |
|   View: English   |      |   View: English   |
|                   |      |   View: German    |
|                   |      |   View: French    |
+-------------------+      +-------------------+
```
- Separate customer bases
- Separate tax/payment/shipping configuration
- Separate product pricing (if price scope = Website)

### Pattern 2: Store Per Category Structure

```
Website: example.com
  |
  +-- Store: Apparel (Root: Apparel Category)
  |     +-- Store View: English
  |     +-- Store View: French
  |
  +-- Store: Electronics (Root: Electronics Category)
        +-- Store View: English
        +-- Store View: French
```
- Same customer base (same website)
- Different navigation trees per store
- Shared language store views but different root categories

### Pattern 3: Store View Per Language Only

```
Website: example.com
  |
  +-- Store: Main Store (Root: Default Category)
        +-- Store View: en  (English)
        +-- Store View: fr  (French)
        +-- Store View: de  (German)
        +-- Store View: es  (Spanish)
```
- Simplest multi-language setup
- One customer base, one catalog structure
- Only display/translation layer differs

> **Exam focus:** Pattern 3 is the most common real-world setup for a single-brand multi-language store. Pattern 1 is used for true multi-brand or multi-region operations with separate customer bases.

---

## 10. Admin Navigation & Setup

### All Stores Overview

```
Admin > Stores > Settings > All Stores
```

This page shows all three tiers in a single hierarchical grid:

```
[Create Website]   [Create Store]   [Create Store View]

WEBSITE         STORE           STORE VIEW
-----------     -----------     -----------
Main Website    Main Store      Default Store View
                                English
                                French
Brand B Site    Brand B Store   Brand B EN
```

### Checking Scope in Config

When viewing any config section, use the **Store View switcher** in the top-left dropdown of the Configuration page:

```
Admin > Stores > Configuration
   [Default Config v]   <-- scope dropdown
   [Main Website v]
   [Default Store View v]
   [English v]
   [French v]
```

The orange **"[STORE VIEW]"** label next to a field indicates it has been overridden at that scope.

### CLI Commands for Store Management

```bash
# List all stores/websites/views
bin/magento store:list

# Output columns: ID | Website ID | Group ID | Name | Code | Sort Order | Is Active
# +----+------------+----------+------------------+------+------------+-----------+
# | ID | Website ID | Group ID | Name             | Code | Sort Order | Is Active |
# +----+------------+----------+------------------+------+------------+-----------+
# | 0  | 0          | 0        | Admin            |      | 0          | 1         |
# | 1  | 1          | 1        | Default Store V. | base | 0          | 1         |
# | 2  | 1          | 1        | French           | fr   | 0          | 1         |
# +----+------------+----------+------------------+------+------------+-----------+

# Set config at specific scope
bin/magento config:set --scope=websites --scope-code=base web/unsecure/base_url https://www.example.com/

# Set config at store view scope
bin/magento config:set --scope=stores --scope-code=fr web/unsecure/base_url https://fr.example.com/

# Show config value with scope
bin/magento config:show --scope=stores --scope-code=fr web/unsecure/base_url
```

> **Exam focus:** The CLI scope flags use **plural** forms: `--scope=websites`, `--scope=stores`. The PHP `ScopeInterface` constants use singular: `SCOPE_WEBSITE`, `SCOPE_STORE`. The `config:set --scope` help text says: "Configuration scope (default, website, or store)".

---

## 11. Common Tricky Exam Scenarios

### Scenario 1: Product Visibility Confusion

> *"A product is not appearing in the French store view. Where do you check?"*

**Answer path:**
1. Check the product is **enabled**
2. Check the product is **assigned to the Website** (not the store view)
3. Check the product's **root category** is within the store's root category tree
4. Check the product's **visibility** attribute is not set to "Not Visible Individually"
5. Check **stock status** (if backorders are disabled)

> **Exam focus:** You CANNOT fix visibility by assigning a product to a store view — there is no such concept. Assignment is always at the **website** level.

---

### Scenario 2: Config Not Inheriting

> *"I changed a setting at Default scope but the Website still shows the old value."*

**Answer:** The Website has an **explicit override** (the "Use Default" checkbox is unchecked). You must navigate to that Website scope in Admin config and check "Use Default" to restore inheritance.

---

### Scenario 3: Customer Can't Log In on Second Website

> *"A customer registered on website A but can't log in on website B."*

**Answer:** Customer accounts are scoped **per website by default**. The customer must register a new account on website B, or the admin must enable **Global** customer account sharing.

---

### Scenario 4: Different Prices Per Country Website

> *"How do you show different prices for US vs EU website?"*

**Answer:**
1. Change the `price` attribute scope from **Global** to **Website**
   (`Stores > Attributes > Product > price > Scope = Website`)
2. Edit the product and switch to the EU website scope to set the EU price

> **Exam focus:** The price attribute is **Global** by default (set by data patch `ChangePriceAttributeDefaultScope`). Changing it to Website scope after data exists requires a **catalog price index reindex**.

---

### Scenario 5: Store Code in URL vs. Separate Domain

| Approach | Store Code in URL | Separate Domain |
|---|---|---|
| Setup complexity | Low | Medium-High |
| SEO clarity | URLs contain `/fr/` path | Clean domain `fr.example.com` |
| SSL certificate | One cert | Separate certs per domain |
| Config location | Web > Url Options | Web > Base URLs per store view |
| Nginx/Apache changes | Minimal | `MAGE_RUN_CODE` per vhost |

---

### Scenario 6: "Use Default" / "Use Website" vs. Explicit Blank

```
Default scope: tax_class = "Taxable Goods"
Website scope: [x] Use Default  -> Inherits "Taxable Goods"
Website scope: [ ] Use Default, value = ""  -> Explicit blank (overrides with empty!)

Store View scope: [x] Use Website  -> Inherits from Website
Store View scope: [ ] Use Website, value = ""  -> Explicit blank override
```

> **Exam focus:** An explicitly saved blank value is a valid override. It does NOT fall back to the parent scope. This is a frequent source of bugs in Magento config.

---

## 12. Quick-Reference Checklist

### Hierarchy & Scope
- [ ] Three tiers: **Website > Store (Group) > Store View** — memorise this order
- [ ] "Store" in Admin = **Store Group** (not a store view)
- [ ] **Configuration** scope order: **Default > Website > Store View** (3 levels, NOT 4 — Store Group is not a config scope)
- [ ] `core_config_data` valid scopes: `'default'`, `'website'`, `'store'` (store view)
- [ ] Lower scope overrides higher scope when inheritance checkbox is unchecked
- [ ] `store_id = 0` is the **Admin store** (never a customer-facing store view)

### What Lives Where
- [ ] **Customer accounts** — scoped to **Website**
- [ ] **Product assignment** — to **Website** (not store view)
- [ ] **Root category** — assigned to **Store (Group)**
- [ ] **Display language / locale** — configured at **Store View**
- [ ] **Base URL** — configured at **Store View**
- [ ] **Base currency** — configured at **Website** (`showInDefault="1" showInWebsite="1"`, no `showInStore`)
- [ ] **Price attribute** — **Global** scope by default (after data patch); can be changed to Website

### Customer Accounts
- [ ] Default sharing = **Per Website** (`customer/account_share/scope` = `1` = SHARE_WEBSITE)
- [ ] Can be changed to **Global** (`0` = SHARE_GLOBAL) in Customer Configuration
- [ ] `customer_entity` table has `website_id` column for scoping
- [ ] Same email address can exist on multiple websites as separate accounts (unique constraint on email + website_id)

### Product Catalog
- [ ] Assign product to website via **Product in Websites** tab
- [ ] Product attribute values (name, description) can be per **Store View**
- [ ] Product navigation visibility filtered by **root category of the Store**
- [ ] You CANNOT assign a product to a specific store view directly
- [ ] EAV attribute scope constants: SCOPE_STORE=0 (store view), SCOPE_GLOBAL=1, SCOPE_WEBSITE=2

### URLs & Routing
- [ ] Store code in URL: `Stores > Config > General > Web > Url Options > Add Store Code to Urls`
- [ ] Base URL per store view: `Stores > Config > General > Web > Base URLs`
- [ ] Server-side routing uses `MAGE_RUN_CODE` + `MAGE_RUN_TYPE` environment variables
- [ ] `MAGE_RUN_TYPE` = `website`, `store` (store view), or `group` (store group)

### PHP & CLI Scope
- [ ] PHP singular: `ScopeInterface::SCOPE_STORE` (= store view), `SCOPE_WEBSITE`, `SCOPE_GROUP`
- [ ] PHP plural: `ScopeInterface::SCOPE_STORES`, `SCOPE_WEBSITES`, `SCOPE_GROUPS` (6 constants total)
- [ ] CLI plural flags: `--scope=stores`, `--scope=websites`
- [ ] `$scopeConfig->getValue($path, ScopeInterface::SCOPE_STORE)` = current store view value
- [ ] `config:set --scope=stores --scope-code=fr` sets value for French store view

### XML Configuration
- [ ] `showInDefault`, `showInWebsite`, `showInStore` control scope editability (`showInStore` = store **view**)
- [ ] Attribute scope options: **Store View** (0), **Global** (1), **Website** (2) — via `ScopedAttributeInterface`
- [ ] Price attribute = Global by default; change requires reindex

### Common Exam Traps
- [ ] Products are assigned to **Website**, NOT to Store View — most common trap
- [ ] Customer accounts are **per Website** by default, not global
- [ ] Inheritance checkbox = inherit; unchecked + blank = explicit blank override (not inherit)
- [ ] At store view level the checkbox says **"Use Website"**, at website level it says **"Use Default"**
- [ ] Changing price attribute scope to Website after data exists requires reindex
- [ ] `SCOPE_STORE` constant refers to **store view**, not store group — in both ScopeInterface and ScopedAttributeInterface
- [ ] CLI `--scope=stores` (plural) vs PHP `SCOPE_STORE` (singular) — different syntax, same level
- [ ] Config scope is 3 levels (Default > Website > Store View) — Store Group is **not** a config scope
- [ ] `store` table column is `is_active`, not `status`

flashcards.question: What is the three-tier scope hierarchy in Magento 2, and what entity lives at each level?
flashcards.answer: The hierarchy is Website > Store (Store Group) > Store View. Websites control customer accounts, payment/shipping methods, and product assignment. Stores (Store Groups) control the root category assignment for navigation. Store Views control display language, locale, currency display, and translated content.
flashcards.hint: The three tiers go from broadest business separation down to language/locale presentation.

flashcards.question: At which scope level are customer accounts managed by default in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: Customer accounts are scoped to the Website by default. The same email can exist as separate accounts on different websites. This is controlled by the 'Share Customer Accounts' setting (config path: `customer/account_share/scope`, default value `1` = SHARE_WEBSITE). It can be changed to Global (`0`) for cross-website sharing.
flashcards.hint: The default behavior isolates customer identities per brand/region entity, not per language view.

flashcards.question: Products in Magento 2 are assigned to which scope level, and how does this affect visibility?
flashcards.answer: Products are assigned to Websites, not to store views or store groups. You cannot assign a product to a specific store view. When assigned to a website, the product becomes visible in all store views under that website. However, actual navigation visibility is further filtered by the store group's root category tree.
flashcards.hint: The assignment happens at the brand/region level — you cannot selectively show a product in one language view but not another under the same parent.

flashcards.question: What are the three configuration scope levels in Magento 2, and how do they differ from the store hierarchy?
flashcards.answer: Configuration scope has three levels: Default (Global) > Website > Store View. Importantly, Store Group is NOT a configuration scope — it only serves as a structural entity for grouping store views and assigning root categories. The `core_config_data` table only stores values for scopes 'default', 'website', and 'store' (which means store view).
flashcards.hint: There's a missing middle tier — the structural grouping entity does not participate in config inheritance.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between checking the 'Use Default' checkbox and saving a blank value at Website scope?
flashcards.answer: Checking 'Use Default' enables inheritance — the value cascades down from the Default scope. Unchecking the checkbox and saving a blank value is an explicit blank override — it does NOT fall back to the parent scope. This is a frequent source of configuration bugs in Magento.
flashcards.hint: One says 'inherit from above,' while the other says 'I want nothing' and blocks inheritance.

flashcards.question: What does the root category assignment on a Store (Store Group) control?
flashcards.answer: The root category assigned to a Store Group determines the entire navigation tree visible on the frontend for that store. Two stores under the same website share customer accounts but can have completely different product navigation trees. A store must have at least one store view to be functional.
flashcards.hint: This assignment controls which products appear in the menu, even if the products are assigned to the same website.

flashcards.question: What is the default scope of the `price` attribute in Magento 2, and what happens when you change it?
flashcards.answer: The `price` attribute is Global scope by default (set by the `ChangePriceAttributeDefaultScope` data patch). This means one price across all websites and store views. Changing it to Website scope allows different prices per website but requires a catalog price index reindex. The `name` and `description` attributes are Store View scope by default.
flashcards.hint: A core data patch overrides the initial scope, and switching it after data exists has indexing consequences.

flashcards.question: How do `MAGE_RUN_CODE` and `MAGE_RUN_TYPE` environment variables work for multi-store routing?
flashcards.answer: These environment variables are set in Apache (`.htaccess`/VirtualHost) or Nginx server blocks to force a specific store or website based on the incoming domain. `MAGE_RUN_CODE` specifies the store/website code, and `MAGE_RUN_TYPE` accepts values `website`, `store` (store view), or `group` (store group) to determine which entity type the code refers to.
flashcards.hint: These server-level variables map incoming domains to specific commerce entities before PHP processing begins.

flashcards.question: What is `store_id = 0` in Magento 2, and why is it significant?
flashcards.answer: `store_id = 0` represents the Admin store — it is never a customer-facing store view. In EAV value tables, `store_id = 0` represents the global/default value that serves as the fallback when no store-view-specific override exists. The first default store view is conventionally `store_id = 1`, but this is not guaranteed.
flashcards.hint: This special ID serves dual duty as both the admin interface identifier and the EAV fallback row.

flashcards.question: What is the naming confusion between ScopeInterface constants and CLI scope flags in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: PHP `ScopeInterface` uses singular constants: `SCOPE_STORE` (means store view), `SCOPE_WEBSITE`, `SCOPE_GROUP`. CLI scope flags use plural forms: `--scope=stores`, `--scope=websites`. Additionally, `SCOPE_STORE` refers to store VIEW, not store group — this is a constant source of confusion in both code and exams.
flashcards.hint: Singular in PHP, plural on the command line — and the word 'store' doesn't mean what you'd expect.

flashcards.question: In the `system.xml` field definition, what do `showInDefault`, `showInWebsite`, and `showInStore` control?
flashcards.answer: These attributes control at which scope level a configuration field is visible and editable in the Admin. `showInDefault="1"` makes it editable at Default (Global) scope, `showInWebsite="1"` at Website scope, and `showInStore="1"` at Store View scope. Note that `showInStore` refers to store VIEW, not store group — this naming is confusingly inconsistent.
flashcards.hint: These XML attributes act as visibility toggles per scope tier in the Admin configuration screens.

flashcards.question: Why might a product not appear in a specific store view, and what are the diagnostic steps?
flashcards.answer: Check: (1) the product is enabled, (2) it is assigned to the correct Website (not store view — there's no such assignment), (3) it belongs to a category within the store's root category tree, (4) its visibility is not 'Not Visible Individually,' and (5) stock status allows display. The most common trap is trying to fix visibility by assigning to a store view, which doesn't exist.
flashcards.hint: Start at the website assignment and work through the category tree and visibility settings — there's no store-view-level product assignment.

flashcards.question: How does the EAV attribute scope constant `SCOPE_STORE = 0` differ from `SCOPE_GLOBAL = 1`?
flashcards.answer: In `ScopedAttributeInterface`, `SCOPE_STORE = 0` means the attribute value can be set per store view (most granular), while `SCOPE_GLOBAL = 1` means one value for all websites and store views. `SCOPE_WEBSITE = 2` allows per-website values. The integer values are counter-intuitive — 0 for most granular, 1 for least — which is a common exam trap.
flashcards.hint: The numeric values are reversed from what you'd expect: the smaller number gives more granular control.

flashcards.question: What is the 'Add Store Code to URLs' setting, and what effect does it have?
flashcards.answer: When enabled at Stores > Configuration > General > Web > Url Options, Magento appends the store view code to the URL path (e.g., `/fr/`, `/de/`). This is one approach to multi-language URLs. The alternative is configuring separate base URLs (subdomains or domains) per store view. Store code in URL requires minimal server configuration compared to separate domains.
flashcards.hint: This setting embeds the language identifier directly in the URL path rather than using separate domains.

flashcards.question: Where is the base currency configured in Magento 2, and at which scope level?
flashcards.answer: Base currency is configured at the Website scope level. It is available in Stores > Configuration > General > Currency Setup. The field has `showInDefault="1"` and `showInWebsite="1"` but no `showInStore`, meaning it cannot be overridden per store view. Display currency (allowed currencies) can differ per store view, but the base currency is always per website.
flashcards.hint: The foundational money denomination is set at the middle tier of the hierarchy, not the most granular one.

studyNotes.title: Day 10 — URL Rewrites & Admin Panel Architecture
studyNotes.content:
# URL Rewrites & Admin Panel Architecture
## Magento 2 Certification Study Notes

---

## Table of Contents

1. [URL Rewrites Overview](#1-url-rewrites-overview)
2. [The url_rewrite Table](#2-the-url_rewrite-table)
3. [Auto-Generated URL Rewrites](#3-auto-generated-url-rewrites)
4. [URL Suffix Configuration](#4-url-suffix-configuration)
5. [Manual URL Rewrite Creation](#5-manual-url-rewrite-creation)
6. [URL Key Changes & Automatic Redirects](#6-url-key-changes--automatic-redirects)
7. [Admin Routing Architecture](#7-admin-routing-architecture)
8. [Admin Menu Configuration](#8-admin-menu-configuration)
9. [ACL for Admin Menu & Controllers](#9-acl-for-admin-menu--controllers)
10. [Tricky Exam Scenarios](#10-tricky-exam-scenarios)
11. [Hands-On: url_rewrite Table Inspection](#11-hands-on-url_rewrite-table-inspection)
12. [Quick-Reference Checklist](#quick-reference-checklist)

---

## 1. URL Rewrites Overview

URL rewrites in Magento 2 translate **user-friendly URLs** (e.g., `/red-shirt.html`) into **internal Magento routes** (e.g., `catalog/product/view/id/42`). This decouples SEO-friendly URLs from the underlying routing system.

### How the Rewrite Process Works

```
Browser Request: /mens/shirts/red-shirt.html
         |
         v
Magento Front Controller
         |
         v
  URL Rewrite Plugin (checks url_rewrite table)
         |
         +---> Match found?
                    |
                  YES --> Route to target_path (internal or redirect)
                    |
                   NO  --> 404 / pass to router
```

- **Exam focus:** URL rewrites are processed **before** standard routing. The `Magento\UrlRewrite\Model\UrlFinderInterface` is responsible for resolving rewrites. It has two methods: `findOneByData(array $data)` and `findAllByData(array $data)`.
- **Exam focus:** The rewrite system supports both **internal forwards** (transparent to the user) and **HTTP redirects** (301/302).

---

## 2. The url_rewrite Table

The central table that stores all URL rewrite mappings is `url_rewrite` in the Magento database.

### Table Schema

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `url_rewrite_id` | int unsigned (PK, auto-increment) | Primary key |
| `entity_type` | varchar(32) | Type of entity: `product`, `category`, `cms-page`, `custom` |
| `entity_id` | int unsigned | ID of the associated entity (product ID, category ID, etc.) |
| `request_path` | varchar(255) | The incoming URL path the user visits (e.g., `mens/shirts/red-shirt.html`) |
| `target_path` | varchar(255) | Internal route or external URL (e.g., `catalog/product/view/id/42`) |
| `redirect_type` | smallint unsigned (default 0) | `0` = no redirect (forward), `301` = permanent, `302` = temporary |
| `store_id` | smallint unsigned | Store view ID this rewrite applies to |
| `description` | varchar(255) | Optional human-readable description |
| `is_autogenerated` | smallint unsigned (default 0) | `1` = auto-generated by Magento, `0` = manually created |
| `metadata` | varchar(255) | Serialized extra data (e.g., category path information) |

**Key constraints:** UNIQUE on `(request_path, store_id)` — a request path can only exist once per store view.

### Sample Records

```sql
-- Product rewrite (transparent forward, no redirect)
SELECT * FROM url_rewrite WHERE entity_type = 'product' LIMIT 3;

-- Result example:
-- url_rewrite_id | entity_type | entity_id | request_path                       | target_path                    | redirect_type | store_id
-- 101            | product     | 42        | mens/shirts/red-shirt.html         | catalog/product/view/id/42     | 0             | 1
-- 102            | product     | 42        | red-shirt.html                     | catalog/product/view/id/42     | 0             | 1

-- Category rewrite
-- 201            | category    | 15        | mens/shirts.html                   | catalog/category/view/id/15    | 0             | 1

-- CMS page rewrite
-- 301            | cms-page    | 3         | about-us                           | cms/page/view/page_id/3        | 0             | 1

-- 301 redirect after URL key change
-- 401            | product     | 42        | old-red-shirt.html                 | red-shirt.html                 | 301           | 1
```

- **Exam focus:** `redirect_type = 0` means an **internal forward** — the URL in the browser does NOT change. The user sees the friendly URL but Magento internally routes to `target_path`.
- **Exam focus:** `entity_type` values are: `product`, `category`, `cms-page`, `custom`. Note the hyphen in `cms-page`. These are defined as constants in `Magento\UrlRewrite\Controller\Adminhtml\Url\Rewrite`.
- **Exam focus:** `is_autogenerated = 1` for system-generated rewrites; manual rewrites have `is_autogenerated = 0`.
- **Exam focus:** Each rewrite is **store-view specific** (`store_id`). A product in 3 store views = 3 (or more) rows.

---

## 3. Auto-Generated URL Rewrites

Magento automatically generates URL rewrites for three entity types when they are saved.

### 3.1 Product URL Rewrites

Products generate rewrites based on their **URL key** attribute.

#### Without Category Path

```
Product URL key: red-shirt
Generated request_path: red-shirt.html
Target path: catalog/product/view/id/42
```

#### With Category Path (when enabled)

```
Product URL key: red-shirt
Category path: mens > shirts
Generated request_paths:
  - red-shirt.html                    (direct, no category)
  - mens/red-shirt.html               (parent category)
  - mens/shirts/red-shirt.html        (full category path)
```

- **Exam focus:** Category path inclusion is controlled by the config: **Stores > Configuration > Catalog > Catalog > Search Engine Optimization > "Use Categories Path for Product URLs"** (config path: `catalog/seo/product_use_categories`, default: `0` = disabled).
- **Exam focus:** When enabled, Magento generates **multiple rows** in `url_rewrite` for each product — one for each category the product belongs to, plus one without any category path.

### 3.2 Category URL Rewrites

Categories generate rewrites based on their **URL key** and their position in the category tree.

```
Category tree:  Default Root (1) > Mens (12) > Shirts (15)

Generated rewrites:
  - mens.html          --> catalog/category/view/id/12
  - mens/shirts.html   --> catalog/category/view/id/15
```

- **Exam focus:** When a **parent category** URL key changes, ALL child category rewrites are regenerated, and all **product rewrites** within those categories are also regenerated.

### 3.3 CMS Page URL Rewrites

CMS pages use their **URL key** field directly.

```
CMS Page URL key: about-us
Generated request_path: about-us
Target path: cms/page/view/page_id/3
```

- **Exam focus:** CMS pages typically do **not** have a suffix (like `.html`) unless configured. Products and categories use configurable suffixes.

### Auto-Generation Trigger Points

```
Product Save  -----> Magento\CatalogUrlRewrite\Observer\ProductProcessUrlRewriteSavingObserver
Category Save -----> Magento\CatalogUrlRewrite\Observer\CategoryProcessUrlRewriteSavingObserver
CMS Page Save -----> Magento\CmsUrlRewrite\Observer\ProcessUrlRewriteSavingObserver
```

---

## 4. URL Suffix Configuration

URL suffixes are configured per entity type in the Admin panel.

### Configuration Path

**Stores > Configuration > Catalog > Catalog > Search Engine Optimization**

| Setting | Default | Config Path |
|---|---|---|
| Product URL Suffix | `.html` | `catalog/seo/product_url_suffix` |
| Category URL Suffix | `.html` | `catalog/seo/category_url_suffix` |

### Behavior

```
URL key:  red-shirt
Suffix:   .html
Result:   red-shirt.html

URL key:  mens/shirts (category)
Suffix:   .html
Result:   mens/shirts.html

URL key:  about-us (CMS)
No suffix configured by default
Result:   about-us
```

- **Exam focus:** Changing the URL suffix triggers a **mass regeneration** of all product/category URL rewrites. Old URLs get 301 redirects automatically.
- **Exam focus:** Suffixes can be set to an **empty string** — in which case URLs have no suffix at all.
- **Exam focus:** Product and category suffixes are configured **independently** of each other.
- **Exam focus:** CMS pages do **not** have a dedicated suffix setting in the same location — their suffix is part of their URL key itself.

---

## 5. Manual URL Rewrite Creation

Administrators can create custom URL rewrites via **Marketing > SEO & Search > URL Rewrites**.

### Types of Manual Rewrites

| Type | redirect_type value | HTTP Status | Use Case |
|---|---|---|---|
| No redirect (forward) | `0` | None (internal) | Alias for an internal page |
| Permanent redirect | `301` | 301 Moved Permanently | Page moved forever |
| Temporary redirect | `302` | 302 Found | Page temporarily moved |
| Custom URL redirect | `301` or `302` | 301/302 | Redirect to any URL |

### Creating a Manual Rewrite in Admin

**Step-by-step:**

1. Navigate to **Marketing > SEO & Search > URL Rewrites**
2. Click **Add URL Rewrite**
3. Select **Create URL Rewrite for**: `Custom`
4. Fill in the form:

```
Store:           Main Website > Default Store View
Request Path:    old-product-path.html
Target Path:     new-product-path.html  (or full URL)
Redirect Type:   Permanent (301)
Description:     Redirect old landing page to new
```

5. Save

### Manual vs. Custom Target Paths

```bash
# Internal target (no domain needed)
target_path: catalog/product/view/id/42

# External target (full URL for external redirect)
target_path: https://example.com/other-page

# Relative internal URL
target_path: new-page.html
```

- **Exam focus:** For **Custom** type rewrites, `entity_type = 'custom'` and `entity_id = 0` in the database.
- **Exam focus:** Manual rewrites have `is_autogenerated = 0`.
- **Exam focus:** You can also create rewrites **for specific entity types** (Product, Category, CMS Page) which links the rewrite to that entity.

---

## 6. URL Key Changes & Automatic Redirects

When a URL key changes, Magento automatically preserves the old URL with a redirect.

### Product URL Key Change Flow

```
BEFORE change:
  url_rewrite: request_path=old-shirt.html --> target_path=catalog/product/view/id/42, redirect_type=0

Admin saves product with new URL key "new-shirt"

AFTER change:
  url_rewrite: request_path=new-shirt.html --> target_path=catalog/product/view/id/42, redirect_type=0  (NEW)
  url_rewrite: request_path=old-shirt.html --> target_path=new-shirt.html, redirect_type=301            (PRESERVED)
```

### Category URL Key Change Flow

```
BEFORE:
  Category "Shirts" URL key: shirts
  Request paths:
    mens/shirts.html      --> catalog/category/view/id/15
    mens/shirts/red-shirt.html --> catalog/product/view/id/42

Admin changes category URL key to "t-shirts"

AFTER:
  NEW rewrites:
    mens/t-shirts.html         --> catalog/category/view/id/15   (new)
    mens/t-shirts/red-shirt.html --> catalog/product/view/id/42  (new)

  301 REDIRECTS created:
    mens/shirts.html           --> mens/t-shirts.html            (301)
    mens/shirts/red-shirt.html --> mens/t-shirts/red-shirt.html  (301)
```

- **Exam focus:** Changing a **category URL key** changes the URL of **ALL products in that category path** (when category paths are enabled). This is a critical exam topic.
- **Exam focus:** Old URLs are **automatically preserved as 301 redirects**. They are NOT deleted.
- **Exam focus:** This behavior is controlled by **"Create Permanent Redirect for URLs if URL Key Changed"** (config path: `catalog/seo/save_rewrites_history`, default: `1` = enabled).
- **Exam focus:** Redirect chains can build up over time if URL keys are changed repeatedly. Regular cleanup of the `url_rewrite` table is a performance best practice.

---

## 7. Admin Routing Architecture

The Magento admin panel uses a dedicated **area** called `adminhtml` with its own routing conventions.

### Admin Area vs. Frontend Area

| Aspect | Frontend | Adminhtml |
|---|---|---|
| Area code | `frontend` | `adminhtml` |
| Base URL | Configured URL | `/admin` (configurable) |
| Routes file | `frontend/routes.xml` | `adminhtml/routes.xml` |
| Controller namespace | `Controller/` | `Controller/Adminhtml/` |
| Layout handles | `frontend` layouts | `adminhtml` layouts |

### 7.1 Admin routes.xml

Location: `<Module>/etc/adminhtml/routes.xml`

```xml
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<config xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:App/etc/routes.xsd">
    <router id="admin">
        <route id="mymodule" frontName="mymodule">
            <module name="Vendor_MyModule" />
        </route>
    </router>
</config>
```

- **Exam focus:** The `router id` for admin routes is `"admin"`, NOT `"standard"` (which is used for frontend).
- **Exam focus:** `frontName` becomes the first segment of the admin URL: `/admin/mymodule/...`

### 7.2 Admin URL Structure

```
/admin/mymodule/items/index

Breakdown:
  /admin         = admin front name (configurable)
  /mymodule      = route frontName (from routes.xml)
  /items         = subdirectory under Controller/Adminhtml/ (lowercased)
  /index         = action class name (lowercased, e.g. Index.php)
```

In Magento 2, each controller is a **single class with one `execute()` method**. The URL segments map to the directory and class name, not to method names.

### 7.3 Admin Controller Namespace

Admin controllers **must** reside in the `Controller/Adminhtml/` directory and extend `\Magento\Backend\App\Action`.

```
app/code/Vendor/MyModule/
  Controller/
    Adminhtml/
      Items/
        Index.php    --> /admin/mymodule/items/index
        Edit.php     --> /admin/mymodule/items/edit
        Save.php     --> /admin/mymodule/items/save
        Delete.php   --> /admin/mymodule/items/delete
```

### 7.4 Admin Controller Example

```php
<?php
namespace Vendor\MyModule\Controller\Adminhtml\Items;

use Magento\Backend\App\Action;
use Magento\Backend\App\Action\Context;
use Magento\Framework\View\Result\PageFactory;

class Index extends Action
{
    /**
     * ACL resource constant - must match acl.xml
     * Default in parent class is 'Magento_Backend::admin'
     */
    const ADMIN_RESOURCE = 'Vendor_MyModule::items';

    /**
     * @var PageFactory
     */
    protected $resultPageFactory;

    public function __construct(
        Context $context,
        PageFactory $resultPageFactory
    ) {
        parent::__construct($context);
        $this->resultPageFactory = $resultPageFactory;
    }

    public function execute()
    {
        $resultPage = $this->resultPageFactory->create();
        $resultPage->setActiveMenu('Vendor_MyModule::items');
        $resultPage->getConfig()->getTitle()->prepend(__('My Items'));
        return $resultPage;
    }
}
```

- **Exam focus:** The `const ADMIN_RESOURCE` defines which ACL resource is required to access the controller. If the current admin user lacks this permission, they receive a **403 Forbidden** response with the `adminhtml_denied` layout rendered.
- **Exam focus:** Admin controllers extend `\Magento\Backend\App\Action`, NOT `\Magento\Framework\App\Action\Action`.
- **Exam focus:** `_isAllowed()` is called automatically by the parent `dispatch()` method. It checks `$this->_authorization->isAllowed(static::ADMIN_RESOURCE)`. If the user is not logged in, they are redirected to `*/auth/login` instead.
- **Exam focus:** The default `ADMIN_RESOURCE` in `AbstractAction` is `'Magento_Backend::admin'` — override it in your controller to require a specific permission.

---

## 8. Admin Menu Configuration

The admin menu is configured via `menu.xml` files.

### File Location

```
<Module>/etc/adminhtml/menu.xml
```

### menu.xml Structure

```xml
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<config xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:module:Magento_Backend:etc/menu.xsd">
    <menu>
        <!-- Top-level menu item -->
        <add id="Vendor_MyModule::top_menu"
             title="My Module"
             module="Vendor_MyModule"
             sortOrder="51"
             resource="Vendor_MyModule::top_menu" />

        <!-- Child menu item -->
        <add id="Vendor_MyModule::items"
             title="Manage Items"
             module="Vendor_MyModule"
             sortOrder="10"
             parent="Vendor_MyModule::top_menu"
             action="mymodule/items/index"
             resource="Vendor_MyModule::items" />

        <!-- Another child item linking to config section -->
        <add id="Vendor_MyModule::config"
             title="Configuration"
             module="Vendor_MyModule"
             sortOrder="20"
             parent="Vendor_MyModule::top_menu"
             action="adminhtml/system_config/edit/section/mymodule"
             resource="Vendor_MyModule::config" />
    </menu>
</config>
```

### menu.xml Attribute Reference

| Attribute | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | Yes | Unique identifier. Convention: `Vendor_Module::identifier` |
| `title` | Yes | Display text in the menu |
| `module` | Yes | Module that owns this menu item (for translation context) |
| `resource` | Yes | ACL resource ID required to see this menu item |
| `sortOrder` | No | Integer for ordering siblings (lower = higher in menu) |
| `parent` | No | `id` of the parent menu item. Omit for top-level items |
| `action` | No | Admin route for the link: `frontName/controller/action`. Omit for parent-only items |
| `dependsOnModule` | No | Only show if this module is enabled |
| `dependsOnConfig` | No | Only show if config value is truthy |
| `toolTip` | No | Hover tooltip text |
| `translate` | No | Space-separated list of attributes to translate |
| `target` | No | Link target (e.g., `_blank`) |

- **Exam focus:** The `action` attribute uses the format `frontName/controller/action` — **without** the `/admin/` prefix.
- **Exam focus:** If `action` is omitted, the menu item is a **parent/group** item and cannot be clicked directly.
- **Exam focus:** The `resource` attribute in `menu.xml` must correspond to a resource defined in `acl.xml`. If the resource doesn't exist in ACL, the menu item is hidden.
- **Exam focus:** Menu items are hidden automatically if the logged-in admin user does not have the required `resource` permission.
- **Exam focus:** Required attributes are: `id`, `title`, `module`, `resource` (4 total).

---

## 9. ACL for Admin Menu & Controllers

Access Control Lists (ACL) define what resources exist and who can access them.

### File Location

```
<Module>/etc/acl.xml
```

### acl.xml Structure

```xml
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<config xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:Acl/etc/acl.xsd">
    <acl>
        <resources>
            <resource id="Magento_Backend::admin">
                <!-- Top-level resource - child of the root admin resource -->
                <resource id="Vendor_MyModule::top_menu"
                          title="My Module"
                          sortOrder="51">

                    <!-- Child resources -->
                    <resource id="Vendor_MyModule::items"
                              title="Manage Items"
                              sortOrder="10" />

                    <resource id="Vendor_MyModule::config"
                              title="Configuration"
                              sortOrder="20" />
                </resource>
            </resource>
        </resources>
    </acl>
</config>
```

### ACL, menu.xml, and Controller: The Three-Way Link

```
acl.xml                          menu.xml                         Controller
-------                          --------                         ----------
resource id=                     resource=                        ADMIN_RESOURCE=
"Vendor_MyModule::items"  <----> "Vendor_MyModule::items"  <----> "Vendor_MyModule::items"
                                 action=
                                 "mymodule/items/index"    -----> Controller/Adminhtml/Items/Index.php
```

- **Exam focus:** All three must use the **same resource ID string** for the permission system to work correctly.
- **Exam focus:** ACL resources must be nested under `Magento_Backend::admin` (directly or indirectly) to appear in the admin role configuration screen.
- **Exam focus:** Admin roles (**System > Permissions > User Roles**) grant access to ACL resources. A user can only access menu items and controllers whose resources are granted to their role.
- **Exam focus:** `Magento_Backend::all` is a sibling of `Magento_Backend::admin` in the Backend acl.xml — it is the "Allow everything" resource that grants full admin access when selected in a role.

### ACL Check Flow

```
Admin user requests /admin/mymodule/items/index
              |
              v
AbstractAction::dispatch() is called
              |
              v
Checks: _isAllowed() → does user's role have "Vendor_MyModule::items"?
              |
         YES  |  NO
          |        |
          v        v
      execute()  403 Forbidden
                 (renders adminhtml_denied layout,
                  or redirects to */auth/login if not logged in)
```

---

## 10. Tricky Exam Scenarios

These are high-probability exam gotchas based on the task description.

### Scenario 1: Category URL Key Change Cascades to Products

> **Question:** An admin changes the URL key of the "Shirts" category from `shirts` to `t-shirts`. The category is nested under "Mens". What happens to the product URLs?

**Answer:**
- All product rewrites that included `/mens/shirts/` in their path are **regenerated** with the new path `/mens/t-shirts/`.
- Old product URLs like `/mens/shirts/red-shirt.html` get **automatic 301 redirects** to `/mens/t-shirts/red-shirt.html`.
- This only applies if **"Use Categories Path for Product URLs"** is enabled (`catalog/seo/product_use_categories = 1`).

- **Exam focus:** This is the most commonly tested URL rewrite scenario. Changing ANY ancestor category URL key cascades changes to all descendant categories AND their products.

### Scenario 2: "Use Categories Path for Product URLs" Setting

> **Question:** A product belongs to two categories: "Mens > Shirts" and "Sale". With category paths enabled, how many rows does the product have in `url_rewrite`?

**Answer:** At minimum **3 rows**:
1. `red-shirt.html` (no category path)
2. `mens/shirts/red-shirt.html` (Mens > Shirts path)
3. `sale/red-shirt.html` (Sale path)

If "Mens" itself is a child of another category, even more rows are generated.

- **Exam focus:** When category path is **disabled**, products only get **1 row** per store view (no category in the path).

### Scenario 3: redirect_type Values

| Value | Meaning | Browser behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `0` | Internal forward / no redirect | URL stays the same in browser |
| `301` | Permanent redirect | Browser updates URL, search engines update index |
| `302` | Temporary redirect | Browser updates URL, search engines keep old URL |

- **Exam focus:** `redirect_type = 0` is **not** a redirect. The user's browser URL does NOT change. Magento internally routes the request.

### Scenario 4: Admin Router vs. Frontend Router

> **Question:** What is the `router id` value in `routes.xml` for an admin module?

**Answer:** `"admin"` — not `"standard"`.

```xml
<!-- Frontend routes.xml -->
<router id="standard">

<!-- Admin routes.xml -->
<router id="admin">
```

### Scenario 5: Menu Item Without Action

> **Question:** A top-level menu item in `menu.xml` has no `action` attribute. What happens when a user clicks it?

**Answer:** It expands to show its children. Top-level items without `action` are **group/container** items only. Clicking them shows the submenu.

### Scenario 6: Missing ACL Resource

> **Question:** A `menu.xml` entry references `resource="Vendor_MyModule::items"` but this ID does not exist in `acl.xml`. What happens?

**Answer:** The menu item is **hidden** from all admin users (including administrators), because the resource cannot be resolved.

---

## 11. Hands-On: url_rewrite Table Inspection

### Step 1: Create a Manual URL Rewrite in Admin

1. Go to **Marketing > SEO & Search > URL Rewrites**
2. Click **Add URL Rewrite**
3. Set values:
   - **Create URL Rewrite for:** Custom
   - **Store:** Default Store View
   - **Request Path:** `test-redirect`
   - **Target Path:** `about-us`
   - **Redirect Type:** Permanent (301)
   - **Description:** Test manual rewrite
4. Click **Save**

### Step 2: Verify in Database

```sql
-- Find the manual rewrite just created
SELECT
    url_rewrite_id,
    entity_type,
    entity_id,
    request_path,
    target_path,
    redirect_type,
    store_id,
    is_autogenerated,
    description
FROM url_rewrite
WHERE request_path = 'test-redirect';
```

Expected result:

```
url_rewrite_id | entity_type | entity_id | request_path    | target_path | redirect_type | store_id | is_autogenerated | description
1042           | custom      | 0         | test-redirect   | about-us    | 301           | 1        | 0                | Test manual rewrite
```

### Step 3: Inspect Auto-Generated Product Rewrites

```sql
-- See all rewrites for a specific product
SELECT
    url_rewrite_id,
    entity_type,
    entity_id,
    request_path,
    target_path,
    redirect_type,
    is_autogenerated,
    metadata
FROM url_rewrite
WHERE entity_type = 'product'
  AND entity_id = 42
ORDER BY redirect_type ASC, request_path ASC;
```

### Step 4: Inspect Category Change Impact

```sql
-- Find 301 redirects (auto-created by URL key changes)
SELECT
    request_path,
    target_path,
    redirect_type,
    entity_type
FROM url_rewrite
WHERE redirect_type = 301
  AND is_autogenerated = 1
ORDER BY url_rewrite_id DESC
LIMIT 20;
```

### Step 5: Count Rewrites Per Entity Type

```sql
-- Overview of all rewrite types in the store
SELECT
    entity_type,
    redirect_type,
    is_autogenerated,
    COUNT(*) as total
FROM url_rewrite
GROUP BY entity_type, redirect_type, is_autogenerated
ORDER BY entity_type, redirect_type;
```

### Step 6: Test the Redirect Behavior

```bash
# Test that the manual redirect works (using curl)
curl -I http://your-magento.local/test-redirect

# Expected response headers:
# HTTP/1.1 301 Moved Permanently
# Location: http://your-magento.local/about-us
```

### Step 7: Simulate URL Key Change

1. Edit a product and change its **URL Key** (e.g., from `blue-widget` to `blue-widget-v2`)
2. Save the product
3. Check the database:

```sql
-- See both the new rewrite and the 301 for the old key
SELECT request_path, target_path, redirect_type, is_autogenerated
FROM url_rewrite
WHERE entity_id = <product_id>
  AND entity_type = 'product'
ORDER BY redirect_type ASC;

-- Result:
-- request_path         | target_path                     | redirect_type | is_autogenerated
-- blue-widget-v2.html  | catalog/product/view/id/XX      | 0             | 1
-- blue-widget.html     | blue-widget-v2.html             | 301           | 1
```

---

## Quick-Reference Checklist

### url_rewrite Table
- [ ] **Entity types:** `product`, `category`, `cms-page`, `custom` (constants in `Magento\UrlRewrite\Controller\Adminhtml\Url\Rewrite`)
- [ ] **redirect_type values:** `0` = internal forward, `301` = permanent, `302` = temporary
- [ ] `redirect_type = 0` does NOT change the browser URL — it is a transparent forward
- [ ] `is_autogenerated = 1` for system-created; `0` for manual rewrites
- [ ] `entity_id = 0` for custom/manual rewrites
- [ ] Each rewrite is store-view specific (`store_id` column)
- [ ] UNIQUE constraint on `(request_path, store_id)`

### Auto-Generated Rewrites
- [ ] **Products:** URL key + optional category path(s)
- [ ] **Categories:** URL key + full parent path
- [ ] **CMS Pages:** URL key (typically no suffix), target: `cms/page/view/page_id/{id}`
- [ ] Category path in product URLs controlled by: `catalog/seo/product_use_categories` (default: `0` = disabled)
- [ ] When category paths are enabled, one product can have **multiple rows** (one per category it belongs to, plus one without category)

### URL Suffixes
- [ ] Product suffix: `catalog/seo/product_url_suffix` (default `.html`)
- [ ] Category suffix: `catalog/seo/category_url_suffix` (default `.html`)
- [ ] Configured at: **Stores > Configuration > Catalog > Catalog > SEO**
- [ ] Changing suffix triggers mass regeneration with 301s for old URLs

### URL Key Changes
- [ ] Changing a **product URL key** creates a 301 from old URL to new URL automatically
- [ ] Changing a **category URL key** cascades: ALL child category URLs AND all product URLs in those categories are regenerated with 301 redirects
- [ ] Controlled by: `catalog/seo/save_rewrites_history` (default: `1` = enabled)
- [ ] Old redirects accumulate in `url_rewrite` — periodic cleanup is a performance best practice

### Admin Routing
- [ ] Admin area code: `adminhtml`
- [ ] Admin routes.xml location: `<Module>/etc/adminhtml/routes.xml`
- [ ] Router ID in admin routes.xml: `"admin"` (frontend uses `"standard"`)
- [ ] Admin URL pattern: `/admin/{frontName}/{controllerDir}/{actionClass}`
- [ ] Admin controllers live in: `Controller/Adminhtml/` namespace
- [ ] Admin controllers extend: `\Magento\Backend\App\Action` (which extends `AbstractAction`)
- [ ] `ADMIN_RESOURCE` constant controls access (default: `'Magento_Backend::admin'`)
- [ ] `_isAllowed()` checks `$this->_authorization->isAllowed(static::ADMIN_RESOURCE)`

### Admin Menu (menu.xml)
- [ ] Location: `<Module>/etc/adminhtml/menu.xml`
- [ ] XSD: `urn:magento:module:Magento_Backend:etc/menu.xsd`
- [ ] Required attributes: `id`, `title`, `module`, `resource` (4 required)
- [ ] Optional attributes: `sortOrder`, `parent`, `action`, `dependsOnModule`, `dependsOnConfig`, `toolTip`, `translate`, `target`
- [ ] `id` convention: `Vendor_Module::identifier`
- [ ] `action` format: `frontName/controller/action` (no `/admin/` prefix)
- [ ] Items without `action` = container/group items (no direct link)
- [ ] `resource` must match an ID in `acl.xml`

### ACL (acl.xml)
- [ ] Location: `<Module>/etc/acl.xml`
- [ ] XSD: `urn:magento:framework:Acl/etc/acl.xsd`
- [ ] Module resources must be nested under `Magento_Backend::admin`
- [ ] `Magento_Backend::all` = "Allow everything" resource (sibling of `::admin`)
- [ ] Resource ID in `acl.xml` = `resource` in `menu.xml` = `ADMIN_RESOURCE` in controller
- [ ] Missing ACL resource = menu item hidden from ALL users
- [ ] Roles configured at: **System > Permissions > User Roles**

### Key Tricky Points (High Exam Probability)
- [ ] Changing a **category** URL key changes URLs of **all products in that category** (if category paths enabled)
- [ ] `redirect_type = 0` = forward, NOT a redirect
- [ ] CMS page entity type is `cms-page` (hyphenated, not underscore)
- [ ] Manual rewrites: `entity_type = 'custom'`, `entity_id = 0`, `is_autogenerated = 0`
- [ ] Admin `router id` = `"admin"`, frontend `router id` = `"standard"`
- [ ] All three files must agree on resource ID: `acl.xml` + `menu.xml` + Controller `ADMIN_RESOURCE`
- [ ] 403 denial renders `adminhtml_denied` layout (not a redirect) for logged-in users

flashcards.question: What is the `router id` value in `routes.xml` for admin routes versus frontend routes?
flashcards.answer: For admin routes, the `router id` is `"admin"`. For frontend routes, it is `"standard"`. Admin routes are declared in `<Module>/etc/adminhtml/routes.xml` and admin controllers must reside in the `Controller/Adminhtml/` directory, extending `\Magento\Backend\App\Action`.
flashcards.hint: The admin area uses a different router identifier than the storefront — it's not 'standard'.

flashcards.question: What is the `redirect_type` column in the `url_rewrite` table, and what do its values mean?
flashcards.answer: `redirect_type = 0` means an internal forward — the URL in the browser does NOT change, and Magento internally routes to the `target_path`. `redirect_type = 301` is a permanent redirect (browser updates URL, search engines update index). `redirect_type = 302` is a temporary redirect (browser updates URL, search engines keep old URL).
flashcards.hint: Zero is not a redirect at all — it's transparent routing. The other two are standard HTTP redirect codes.

flashcards.question: What happens to product URLs when a parent category's URL key is changed with category paths enabled?
flashcards.answer: All product rewrites that included the old category path are regenerated with the new path. Old product URLs get automatic 301 redirects to the new URLs. This cascading effect applies to all descendant categories and their products. For example, changing 'shirts' to 't-shirts' updates all products under `/mens/shirts/` to `/mens/t-shirts/`.
flashcards.hint: A change at the category level cascades downward through the entire tree to every product in those categories.

flashcards.question: What are the four `entity_type` values in the `url_rewrite` table?
flashcards.answer: The four entity types are `product`, `category`, `cms-page`, and `custom`. Note that `cms-page` uses a hyphen, not an underscore. Custom/manual rewrites use `entity_type = 'custom'` with `entity_id = 0` and `is_autogenerated = 0`. These are defined as constants in `Magento\UrlRewrite\Controller\Adminhtml\Url\Rewrite`.
flashcards.hint: Three correspond to built-in content types (one hyphenated), and the fourth covers anything manually created.

flashcards.question: How do `acl.xml`, `menu.xml`, and the controller's `ADMIN_RESOURCE` constant work together?
flashcards.answer: All three must use the same resource ID string (e.g., `Vendor_MyModule::items`). `acl.xml` defines the resource in the permission tree. `menu.xml` references that resource to control menu item visibility. The controller's `ADMIN_RESOURCE` constant is checked by `_isAllowed()` during dispatch. If any of these is missing or mismatched, access fails.
flashcards.hint: It's a three-way handshake — the same string must appear in three different XML/PHP files for the permission system to work.

flashcards.question: What controls whether Magento generates category paths in product URLs, and how many `url_rewrite` rows does a product get?
flashcards.answer: The config setting `catalog/seo/product_use_categories` (default: `0` = disabled) controls this. When disabled, a product gets 1 row per store view. When enabled, it gets multiple rows: one without category path, plus one for each category the product belongs to. A product in two categories would get at minimum 3 rows.
flashcards.hint: A single config toggle can multiply the number of database rows per product significantly.

flashcards.question: What are the four required attributes for a `menu.xml` item in Magento 2 Admin?
flashcards.answer: The four required attributes are `id` (unique identifier, convention: `Vendor_Module::identifier`), `title` (display text), `module` (owning module for translation context), and `resource` (ACL resource ID required to see the item). Optional attributes include `sortOrder`, `parent`, `action`, `dependsOnModule`, and `dependsOnConfig`.
flashcards.hint: You need an identifier, a label, a module owner, and a permission reference — everything else is optional.

flashcards.question: How does the `action` attribute format work in `menu.xml`, and what happens if it's omitted?
flashcards.answer: The `action` attribute uses the format `frontName/controller/action` without the `/admin/` prefix (e.g., `mymodule/items/index`). If `action` is omitted, the menu item becomes a parent/group container item that cannot be clicked directly — it only expands to show child items.
flashcards.hint: No prefix needed for the admin base path, and leaving it out turns the item into just a folder.

flashcards.question: What happens when a product's URL key is changed in the Magento Admin?
flashcards.answer: Magento creates a new `url_rewrite` row with the new URL key as `request_path` pointing to the internal target path (`redirect_type = 0`). The old URL key is preserved as a 301 redirect pointing to the new URL. This behavior is controlled by `catalog/seo/save_rewrites_history` (default: `1` = enabled). Redirect chains can accumulate over time.
flashcards.hint: The old URL doesn't disappear — it gets a permanent redirect entry so existing links and search engine indexes continue to work.

flashcards.question: What happens when a `menu.xml` entry references a resource ID that doesn't exist in `acl.xml`?
flashcards.answer: The menu item is hidden from ALL admin users, including administrators with full access. The resource cannot be resolved in the permission system, so no role can be granted access to it. This silently breaks the menu item without any error — a common debugging challenge.
flashcards.hint: If the permission definition doesn't exist, no one can be granted it, making the item invisible to everyone.

flashcards.question: What is the unique constraint on the `url_rewrite` table, and why is it significant?
flashcards.answer: The unique constraint is on `(request_path, store_id)` — a request path can only exist once per store view. This means the same URL path can exist for different store views but not duplicated within one. Each rewrite is store-view specific, so a product in 3 store views generates at least 3 rows.
flashcards.hint: The combination of the incoming path and the language/locale identifier must be unique.

flashcards.question: What base class must admin controllers extend, and what constant controls access?
flashcards.answer: Admin controllers must extend `\Magento\Backend\App\Action` (not `\Magento\Framework\App\Action\Action`). The `ADMIN_RESOURCE` constant defines which ACL resource is required. The default value from the parent class is `'Magento_Backend::admin'`. The `_isAllowed()` method is called automatically during `dispatch()` and checks this constant.
flashcards.hint: There's a specific backend action class (not the generic one), and a class constant controls the permission check.

flashcards.question: What URL suffix settings exist for products and categories, and how do CMS pages differ?
flashcards.answer: Products use `catalog/seo/product_url_suffix` (default `.html`) and categories use `catalog/seo/category_url_suffix` (default `.html`). They are configured independently. CMS pages do not have a dedicated suffix setting — their suffix is part of their URL key itself. Changing a suffix triggers mass regeneration of all affected URL rewrites with 301 redirects.
flashcards.hint: Two entity types have configurable suffixes in the same config section, but the third type handles it differently.

flashcards.question: How are URL rewrites processed in relation to Magento's standard routing system?
flashcards.answer: URL rewrites are processed BEFORE standard routing. The `Magento\UrlRewrite\Model\UrlFinderInterface` resolves rewrites using `findOneByData(array $data)` and `findAllByData(array $data)`. If a match is found, the request is either forwarded internally (redirect_type=0) or redirected via HTTP (301/302). If no match is found, the request passes to the standard router.
flashcards.hint: The rewrite system gets first look at every incoming request, before the normal controller routing kicks in.

flashcards.question: What is the admin URL structure in Magento 2, and how do controller directories map to URL segments?
flashcards.answer: Admin URLs follow the pattern `/admin/{frontName}/{controllerDir}/{actionClass}`. The `/admin` prefix is configurable. The `frontName` comes from `routes.xml`. Controller directories under `Controller/Adminhtml/` map to URL segments (lowercased). Each controller is a single class with one `execute()` method — URL segments map to directory and class names, not method names.
flashcards.hint: Each URL segment corresponds to a directory level under the admin controller namespace, with the final segment being the class name.

studyNotes.title: Day 11 — Attributes & Attribute Sets
studyNotes.content:
# Magento 2 Certification Study Notes
## Attributes & Attribute Sets — EAV Architecture

**Goal:** Week 2 — Architecture: DI, Plugins, Caching, Stores & Admin
**Date:** Jun 5

---

## Table of Contents

1. [EAV Architecture Overview](#1-eav-architecture-overview)
2. [Entity Types](#2-entity-types)
3. [Attribute Data Types](#3-attribute-data-types)
4. [Attribute Scope](#4-attribute-scope)
5. [Attribute Sets and Attribute Groups](#5-attribute-sets-and-attribute-groups)
6. [Custom Attribute Creation via DataPatch](#6-custom-attribute-creation-via-datapatch)
7. [Frontend Model, Backend Model, Source Model](#7-frontend-model-backend-model-source-model)
8. [Searchable, Filterable, and Comparable Flags](#8-searchable-filterable-and-comparable-flags)
9. [Swatch Attributes](#9-swatch-attributes)
10. [Database Schema: EAV Tables](#10-database-schema-eav-tables)
11. [Tricky Concepts & Edge Cases](#11-tricky-concepts--edge-cases)
12. [Hands-On: DataPatch on local-instance](#12-hands-on-datapatch-on-local-instance)
13. [Quick-Reference Checklist](#quick-reference-checklist)

---

## 1. EAV Architecture Overview

**Entity-Attribute-Value (EAV)** is a data modelling pattern used in Magento 2 for flexible, extensible entities. Instead of a single wide table, data is stored across multiple narrow tables.

```
Traditional (flat table):
+----+----------+-------+----------+
| id | name     | color | material |
+----+----------+-------+----------+
| 1  | T-Shirt  | Red   | Cotton   |
+----+----------+-------+----------+

EAV (three tables):
entity table:          attribute table:        value table:
+----+----------+      +------+----------+     +----+------+-------+
| id | sku      |      | a_id | code     |     | id | a_id | value |
+----+----------+      +------+----------+     +----+------+-------+
| 1  | MH01     |      | 92   | color    |     | 1  | 92   | Red   |
+----+----------+      | 93   | material |     | 2  | 93   | Cotton|
                       +------+----------+     +----+------+-------+
```

### Why EAV?

| Concern | Flat Table | EAV |
|---|---|---|
| Adding new attributes | Requires schema change (ALTER TABLE) | Insert a row in `eav_attribute` |
| Storing sparse data | Many NULL columns | Only stores non-null values |
| Multi-store values | Complex joins | Separate value rows per store |
| Query performance | Fast (single join) | Slower (many joins) — Flat tables mitigate this |

- **Exam focus:** Magento uses EAV to allow merchants to add custom attributes without altering core database schema. This is a fundamental architectural decision.
- **Exam focus:** EAV is *not* used for all entities. Orders, for example, use flat tables for performance — `sales_order`, `sales_order_item`, etc.

---

## 2. Entity Types

Each EAV-enabled entity has a registered **entity type** in the `eav_entity_type` table. The entity type code identifies which entity class, tables, and attribute sets belong to it.

### Core Entity Types

| Entity Type Code | Description | Main Table |
|---|---|---|
| `catalog_product` | Products | `catalog_product_entity` |
| `catalog_category` | Categories | `catalog_category_entity` |
| `customer` | Customer accounts | `customer_entity` |
| `customer_address` | Customer addresses | `customer_address_entity` |
| `order` | Sales orders | `sales_order` (flat — *not true EAV*) |

- **Exam focus:** `catalog_product` and `catalog_category` are the primary EAV entities tested. Customer and customer_address are also EAV. Orders use a **flat table** architecture, NOT EAV.
- **Exam focus:** Know the entity type *codes* exactly — they are passed as strings to `EavSetupFactory` methods.

### How Entity Types Are Registered

Entity types are registered in `eav_entity_type` DB table, seeded by core setup scripts and referenced in code like:

```php
$eavSetup->getEntityTypeId('catalog_product');
// Returns integer ID, e.g., 4
```

---

## 3. Attribute Data Types

An attribute's **type** determines both the input widget in the admin and the backend database column type used for storing values.

### Complete Attribute Type Reference

| `input` (frontend_input) | PHP/DB Type | Value Table Used | Admin Widget |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | varchar | `*_entity_varchar` | Single-line text input |
| `textarea` | text | `*_entity_text` | Multi-line textarea |
| `date` | datetime | `*_entity_datetime` | Date picker |
| `boolean` | int | `*_entity_int` | Yes/No dropdown |
| `select` | int | `*_entity_int` | Dropdown (single option) |
| `multiselect` | varchar | `*_entity_varchar` | Multi-select list |
| `price` | decimal | `*_entity_decimal` | Price input with currency |
| `media_image` | varchar | `*_entity_varchar` | Image uploader |
| `static` | — | Main entity table column | N/A (dedicated column) |
| `weight` | decimal | `*_entity_decimal` | Numeric input |
| `gallery` | varchar | — | Media gallery |

> The `*` prefix in table names is replaced by the entity type prefix, e.g., `catalog_product_entity_varchar`.

- **Exam focus:** `static` type attributes are stored in the **main entity table** (e.g., `catalog_product_entity`) as actual columns — NOT in the EAV value tables. Examples: `sku`, `created_at`.
- **Exam focus:** `select` stores the **option ID** (int) in the value table, not the text label. Labels are stored in `eav_attribute_option` and `eav_attribute_option_value`.
- **Exam focus:** `multiselect` stores a **comma-separated string** of option IDs in the varchar table.
- **Exam focus:** `boolean` stores `0` or `1` as an int.

### Value Table Mapping

```
catalog_product_entity_varchar   -> text, multiselect, media_image
catalog_product_entity_int       -> boolean, select
catalog_product_entity_decimal   -> price, weight
catalog_product_entity_text      -> textarea
catalog_product_entity_datetime  -> date
catalog_product_entity           -> static (directly in entity row)
```

---

## 4. Attribute Scope

Attribute scope controls at which level a value can be overridden in a multi-store Magento installation.

### Scope Levels

```
Global Scope:
  +-----------------------------------+
  |  Default (store_id = 0)           |
  |  ONE value for ALL store views    |
  +-----------------------------------+

Website Scope:
  +-----------------------------------+
  |  Default (store_id = 0)           |
  |    +-----------------------------+|
  |    | Website 1                   ||
  |    |   Store View A  (inherits)  ||
  |    |   Store View B  (inherits)  ||
  |    +-----------------------------+|
  +-----------------------------------+

Store View Scope:
  +-----------------------------------+
  |  Default (store_id = 0)           |
  |    Store View A  (own value)      |
  |    Store View B  (different value)|
  +-----------------------------------+
```

### Scope Constants

```php
// Defined in \Magento\Eav\Model\Entity\Attribute\ScopedAttributeInterface
const SCOPE_STORE   = 0; // Store View scope
const SCOPE_GLOBAL  = 1; // Global scope
const SCOPE_WEBSITE = 2; // Website scope
```

> **Note:** The integer value `0` for STORE and `1` for GLOBAL is counter-intuitive and a common exam trap!

### Scope in addAttribute()

```php
$eavSetup->addAttribute('catalog_product', 'my_attribute', [
    'global' => \Magento\Eav\Model\Entity\Attribute\ScopedAttributeInterface::SCOPE_STORE,
    // ...
]);
```

### Scope Behavior Summary

| Scope | `is_global` value | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Global | `1` | Same value for all websites and store views. Cannot be overridden per store. |
| Website | `2` | Can be set per website; all store views under that website share it. |
| Store View | `0` | Can be set per store view. Most used for translations/localized content. |

- **Exam focus:** `store_id = 0` in the value tables always represents the **default/global** row. When a store view has no override, it falls back to `store_id = 0`.
- **Exam focus:** Product **name**, **description**, and **meta** attributes are Store View scope by default (enabling translations). Product **price** is Global scope (a core data patch `ChangePriceAttributeDefaultScope` changes it from Website to Global). Product **status** is **Website** scope by default.
- **Exam focus:** Changing attribute scope from Global to Store View requires running `bin/magento catalog:product:attributes:cleanup` and may cause **data inconsistency** — the existing single global value must be duplicated to each store view.

## 5. Attribute Sets and Attribute Groups

### Attribute Sets

An **attribute set** is a named collection of attributes organized into groups, applied to products of a specific entity type. Every product belongs to exactly one attribute set.

```
Attribute Set: "Clothing"
  +----------------------------------+
  | Group: General                   |
  |   - name, sku, description       |
  +----------------------------------+
  | Group: Design                    |
  |   - color, size, material        |
  +----------------------------------+
  | Group: Prices                    |
  |   - price, special_price         |
  +----------------------------------+
```

### Attribute Groups

An **attribute group** is a tab/section within an attribute set that logically groups related attributes on the admin product form. Groups are purely organizational — they don't affect data storage.

### Key Database Tables

| Table | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `eav_attribute_set` | Stores attribute set definitions |
| `eav_attribute_group` | Stores groups within sets |
| `eav_entity_attribute` | Maps attributes to sets/groups |
| `eav_attribute` | Stores attribute definitions |

### Retrieving Sets Programmatically

```php
use Magento\Eav\Api\AttributeSetRepositoryInterface;
use Magento\Framework\Api\SearchCriteriaBuilder;

$searchCriteria = $this->searchCriteriaBuilder
    ->addFilter('entity_type_id', $entityTypeId)
    ->create();

$attributeSets = $this->attributeSetRepository->getList($searchCriteria);
```

- **Exam focus:** The **Default** attribute set is created automatically for each entity type. Custom attribute sets extend the Default set.
- **Exam focus:** All EAV entity types have attribute sets (`customer` has `ATTRIBUTE_SET_ID_CUSTOMER = 1`, `customer_address` has `ATTRIBUTE_SET_ID_ADDRESS = 2`). However, merchant-managed custom attribute sets (creating/editing sets via admin UI) are a **catalog-only** feature.
- **Exam focus:** When you create a custom attribute and assign it to `All Attribute Sets: true` in the setup script, it appears in ALL existing attribute sets.
