### 10.1 Complete .magento.app.yaml (Production-Ready)

```yaml
name: mymagento
type: php:8.2

build:
    flavor: none

variables:
    env:
        CONFIG__DEFAULT__GENERAL__LOCALE__TIMEZONE: 'America/Chicago'

dependencies:
    php:
        composer/composer: '^2.0'

runtime:
    extensions:
        - xsl
        - sodium
        - redis

disk: 5120

mounts:
    "var":
        source: local
        source_path: var
    "app/etc":
        source: local
        source_path: app/etc
    "pub/media":
        source: local
        source_path: media
    "pub/static":
        source: local
        source_path: static
    "generated":
        source: local
        source_path: generated
    "pub/export":
        source: local
        source_path: export

hooks:
    build: |
        set -e
        php ./vendor/bin/ece-tools run scenario/build/generate.xml
        php ./vendor/bin/ece-tools run scenario/build/transfer.xml
    deploy: |
        php ./vendor/bin/ece-tools run scenario/deploy.xml
    post_deploy: |
        php ./vendor/bin/ece-tools run scenario/post-deploy.xml

relationships:
    database: "mysql:mysql"
    redis: "redis:redis"
    redis-session: "redis-session:redis"
    opensearch: "opensearch:opensearch"
    rabbitmq: "rabbitmq:amqp"

workers:
    queue:
        commands:
            start: |
                php /app/bin/magento queue:consumers:start \
                    async.operations.all \
                    --single-thread \
                    --max-messages=10000

web:
    locations:
        "/":
            root: "pub"
            passthru: "/index.php"
            index:
                - index.php
            expires: -1
            scripts: true
            allow: false
            rules:
                \.(css|js|map|hbs|gif|jpe?g|png|tiff|wbmp|ico|jng|bmp|svgz|midi?|mp?ga|mp2|mp3|m4a|ra|weba|ogg|midi?|mp4|m4v|mpe?g|mpe|ogv|mov|webm|flv|mng|asx|asf|wmv|avi|ogx|swf|jar|ttf|eot|woff|otf|svg|woff2)$:
                    allow: true
            headers:
                X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN
                X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
                X-XSS-Protection: 1;mode=block
        "/media":
            root: "pub/media"
            allow: true
            scripts: false
            expires: 1y
            passthru: "/get.php"
        "/static":
            root: "pub/static"
            allow: true
            scripts: false
            expires: 1y
            passthru: "/front-static.php"
            rules:
                ^/static/version\d+/(.*)$:
                    passthru: "/static/$1"
```

## Quick-Reference Checklist

### .magento.app.yaml

- [ ] `name:` must exactly match the upstream name in `routes.yaml`
- [ ] `type:` sets the PHP version (e.g., `php:8.2`) — changes require full rebuild
- [ ] `disk:` is in MB, cannot be decreased, applies to the app container only
- [ ] **Mounts** are required for writable directories: `var`, `app/etc`, `pub/media`, `pub/static`, `generated`
- [ ] **Build hook** has NO access to services (no database, no Redis)
- [ ] **Deploy hook** runs while the site is in maintenance mode, has service access
- [ ] **Post-deploy hook** runs while the site is live, failures do NOT cause rollback
- [ ] **Relationships** format: `local_alias: "service_name:endpoint"`
- [ ] **Workers** are always-running daemons, preferred over cron for queue consumers
- [ ] Workers have their own container and do NOT serve HTTP traffic

### .magento/services.yaml

- [ ] Service type format: `name:version` (e.g., `mysql:10.6`, `redis:7.0`)
- [ ] **Redis does NOT require `disk:`** — it is in-memory
- [ ] MySQL, OpenSearch, RabbitMQ **require `disk:`**
- [ ] **Disk size CANNOT be decreased** — only increased
- [ ] Use two Redis instances: one for cache, one for sessions
- [ ] Disk values are in MB (`5120` = 5 GB)

### .magento/routes.yaml

- [ ] Route types: `upstream` (send to app) and `redirect` (HTTP redirect)
- [ ] `{default}` placeholder = primary environment domain
- [ ] Upstream format: `app_name:http` — app_name must match `.magento.app.yaml` `name:`
- [ ] HTTP → HTTPS redirect: `type: redirect` pointing to https version
- [ ] WWW → non-WWW: `type: redirect` from `www.{default}` to `{default}`

### .magento.env.yaml

- [ ] Four stage scopes: `global`, `build`, `deploy`, `post_deploy`
- [ ] `global` applies to ALL stages
- [ ] `SCD_ON_DEMAND: true` = generate static files on first request (good for dev, bad for prod)
- [ ] `SKIP_SCD: true` = skip static content generation entirely (dangerous for prod)
- [ ] SCD strategies: `quick` (default), `standard`, `compact`
- [ ] `CRON_CONSUMERS_RUNNER` — set `cron_run: false` if using workers
- [ ] `CACHE_CONFIGURATION` — configures Redis cache backend
- [ ] `SESSION_CONFIGURATION` — configures Redis session storage
- [ ] Sessions should use a **different Redis database** than cache to prevent logout on flush

### Environment Variables

- [ ] **Project-level** variables apply to ALL environments
- [ ] **Environment-level** variables apply to one environment + children
- [ ] **Sensitive** variables are hidden after creation — cannot be retrieved
- [ ] Variable override order: environment-level > project-level > defaults
- [ ] Pro environments: `.magento.env.yaml` managed via **CLI/UI**, NOT git
- [ ] Starter environments: `.magento.env.yaml` managed via **git commit and push**

### app/etc/env.php

- [ ] **Auto-generated** by ECE-Tools during deploy — NEVER manually edit
- [ ] **Not committed to git** (in `.gitignore`)
- [ ] Regenerated on every deployment
- [ ] Contains DB credentials, Redis config, cache config — all from `MAGENTO_CLOUD_RELATIONSHIPS`
- [ ] Use `.magento.env.yaml` variables to influence its content

### Pro vs Starter

- [ ] Pro: `.magento.env.yaml` changes via Cloud CLI or Web UI (no git commit needed)
- [ ] Starter: `.magento.env.yaml` changes via git commit and push
- [ ] Pro has 3 fixed tiers: Integration → Staging → Production
- [ ] Starter has up to 4 environments under master
- [ ] Pro: variables set on Staging do NOT auto-propagate to Production

### Common Exam Traps

- [ ] You **cannot decrease** service disk size
- [ ] Redis **does not need disk** in services.yaml
- [ ] Build hook **cannot access database** or other services
- [ ] `app/etc/env.php` is **regenerated every deploy** — manual edits are lost
- [ ] On Pro, **committing `.magento.env.yaml`** to git does not affect Staging/Production
- [ ] Workers and `CRON_CONSUMERS_RUNNER` can **conflict** — disable cron_run when using workers
- [ ] `{default}` in routes.yaml is a **placeholder** replaced at runtime with actual domain
- [ ] Post-deploy hook failures **do not roll back** the deployment — site remains live

flashcards.question: What are the three YAML configuration files that define a Cloud project's infrastructure, and what does each control?
flashcards.answer: .magento.app.yaml is the primary application container definition controlling PHP version, hooks, mounts, crons, relationships, and workers. .magento/services.yaml defines available infrastructure services (MySQL, Redis, OpenSearch, RabbitMQ) with their types and disk allocations. .magento/routes.yaml defines URL routing rules -- how HTTP/HTTPS traffic is routed to the application or redirected. All three are version-controlled in git.
flashcards.hint: Three YAML files work together: one for the app, one for services, and one for URL routing.

flashcards.question: What is the critical difference between how .magento.env.yaml is managed on Pro versus Starter plans?
flashcards.answer: On Pro, .magento.env.yaml changes for staging and production are managed via the Cloud CLI (magento-cloud variable:create) or the Project Web UI -- NOT through git commits. Changes do not require a git commit. On Starter, .magento.env.yaml is committed directly to git and changes are applied by committing and pushing the file. Attempting to commit .magento.env.yaml on Pro and expecting it to change staging/production behavior is a common mistake.
flashcards.hint: The management method differs by plan -- one uses CLI/UI, the other uses version control.

flashcards.question: Why should you never manually edit app/etc/env.php in an Adobe Commerce Cloud environment?
flashcards.answer: app/etc/env.php is automatically generated by ECE-Tools during each deploy phase -- manual changes are overwritten on every deployment. Credentials are injected from MAGENTO_CLOUD_RELATIONSHIPS environment variable at deploy time. The file is not committed to git (it is in .gitignore). The correct approach is to use .magento.env.yaml variables (SESSION_CONFIGURATION, CACHE_CONFIGURATION, etc.) or environment-level variables to influence its generated content.
flashcards.hint: This file is regenerated from environment data during every deployment cycle.

flashcards.question: What are the three SCD-related variables in .magento.env.yaml, and how do they differ?
flashcards.answer: SCD_STRATEGY (quick/standard/compact) controls the deployment strategy -- 'quick' deploys per module (default), 'standard' per locale/theme, and 'compact' saves disk by symlinking shared files. SCD_ON_DEMAND (true/false) generates static files on first HTTP request rather than during deployment -- good for dev environments but bad for production due to first-request latency. SKIP_SCD (true/false) skips static content generation entirely -- the site will be broken if static files don't exist.
flashcards.hint: One controls how, one controls when, and one controls whether static content is generated at all.

flashcards.question: Why does Redis NOT require a disk allocation in services.yaml while MySQL and OpenSearch do?
flashcards.answer: Redis is an in-memory data store -- it does not persist data to disk (at least not in the same way database services do). MySQL, OpenSearch, and RabbitMQ all require disk allocations because they persist data to disk storage. Specifying a disk value for Redis is unnecessary and may cause warnings. Additionally, service disk sizes can NEVER be decreased once set -- they can only be increased, so plan carefully.
flashcards.hint: The storage model of the service determines whether disk allocation is needed.

flashcards.question: How do relationships in .magento.app.yaml connect the application to services defined in services.yaml?
flashcards.answer: The relationships section maps a local alias to a service endpoint. The format is local_alias: 'service_name:endpoint_name'. For example, 'database: mysql:mysql' maps the alias 'database' to the 'mysql' service's 'mysql' endpoint. Magento uses these aliases to find connection credentials via the MAGENTO_CLOUD_RELATIONSHIPS environment variable. If the alias doesn't match what Magento expects, connections fail.
flashcards.hint: A mapping connects application-level service names to the infrastructure services defined elsewhere.

flashcards.question: What are workers in .magento.app.yaml, and how do they differ from CRON_CONSUMERS_RUNNER?
flashcards.answer: Workers are dedicated always-running daemon processes in their own container, separate from the web container. They are the preferred Cloud-native approach for message queue consumers and auto-restart on crash. CRON_CONSUMERS_RUNNER (configured in .magento.env.yaml) runs consumers via cron triggers on a schedule. When using workers, you should set cron_run: false in CRON_CONSUMERS_RUNNER to avoid conflicts. Workers do NOT serve HTTP requests.
flashcards.hint: One runs continuously in its own container; the other is triggered by the scheduler.

flashcards.question: In routes.yaml, what must the upstream value exactly match, and what does {default} represent?
flashcards.answer: The upstream value format is app_name:http, where app_name must exactly match the name: field in .magento.app.yaml. A mismatch causes routing failures. The {default} placeholder is automatically replaced with the primary domain of the environment -- in production it becomes example.com, in staging/integration it becomes something like branch-name.abc123.us-4.magentosite.cloud. Route types are either 'upstream' (send to app) or 'redirect' (HTTP redirect).
flashcards.hint: The routing configuration references the application by name and uses a dynamic domain placeholder.

flashcards.question: Why should sessions use a different Redis database number than cache in Cloud environments?
flashcards.answer: Sessions should use a separate Redis database number (e.g., database 2) from cache (databases 0 and 1) to prevent cache flushes from clearing customer sessions and logging out users. When Magento flushes the cache (e.g., during deployment or admin cache management), if sessions share the same Redis database, all session data would also be wiped. Using separate databases (or better yet, separate Redis instances) provides complete isolation.
flashcards.hint: A cache management operation could have unintended side effects on user authentication state.

flashcards.question: What are the four stage scopes in .magento.env.yaml, and how does the global scope interact with the others?
flashcards.answer: The four stage scopes are: global (applied to all stages), build (applied only during build hook), deploy (applied during deploy hook), and post_deploy (applied during post-deploy hook). Variables set in the global scope serve as defaults for all stages. Stage-specific settings override global settings. For example, SCD_ON_DEMAND set in global applies everywhere, but setting it differently in the build stage would override just for build.
flashcards.hint: One scope acts as a default for all phases, while the others target specific deployment phases.

flashcards.question: What happens if a developer puts setup:upgrade in the build hook instead of the deploy hook?
flashcards.answer: It will fail because services (database) are not available during the build hook. The setup:upgrade command requires database access to run migrations, check schema versions, and apply data patches. Database operations must go in the deploy hook, where services are available and the site is in maintenance mode. The build hook is only for operations that don't need services: composer install, DI compilation, and SCD generation.
flashcards.hint: A command that needs to read and write to the database cannot run in a phase without database access.

flashcards.question: How do sensitive variables work in Adobe Commerce Cloud, and what makes them different from regular variables?
flashcards.answer: Sensitive variables are created with --sensitive true and become write-only after being set -- you cannot retrieve the value via CLI or UI, only overwrite or delete them. They are never stored in git regardless of where .magento.env.yaml is managed. You can also control their visibility during build (--visible-build) and runtime (--visible-runtime). Regular variables can be read back at any time. Sensitive variables are ideal for API keys, passwords, and other secrets.
flashcards.hint: Once created, the value becomes unreadable -- it can only be replaced or removed.
